items.why: OD-PACKAGE-001 measured PackageKind and PackageId declared and consumed nowhere, and found no package manifest exists on disk anywhere in this workspace. It laid out four steps and named the first as items 1 and 2 together: a declared manifest on disk carrying a PackageId, a PackageKind and PKG-007's four version domains as four distinct fields, plus a reader that refuses what it cannot resolve in the shape nomos-spec-store's registration reader already demonstrates -- landing together, since a manifest with no reader would be the finding reproduced one level up. The record names nomos-lang-rust and nomos-lang-rust-scan as the natural first subject: a LanguagePackage that registers both as providers. Steps 3 (a rule citing its contract version) and 4 (the publish question, already settled) are explicitly out of scope.
items.done_when: A new crate declares a LanguagePackage manifest format: PackageId, PackageKind (must serialize/deserialize as PackageKind::LanguagePackage), and PKG-007's four version domains as four distinct fields -- package version, Nomos protocol range, supported language/dialect versions, provider/tool versions -- none collapsed into another, plus which ProviderIds it registers. A reader parses that format from a file or string and produces either a resolved typed manifest or a typed refusal naming which malformed case occurred (missing field, a PackageKind that is not LanguagePackage where one is required, a version domain that cannot resolve, an unresolvable ProviderId reference) -- nothing silently defaulted or skipped. A real manifest file on disk registers this workspace's own Rust LanguagePackage against nomos-lang-rust and nomos-lang-rust-scan's actual PROVIDER constants, with real distinct values for all four version domains (not a Cargo version copied into more than one). Tests prove the reader round-trips that real manifest and refuses each named malformed case. The crate joins Cargo.toml, README.md's band table and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs at a band above nomos-lang-rust/nomos-lang-rust-scan (25), and tests/contract/surface/ gains its blessed public-surface snapshot. nomos-contracts itself is untouched -- PackageId and PackageKind are read-only from the new crate.

items.title: nomos-ledger's Finish never gives a predicate an idle bound distinct from its wall bound
items.why: OD-PLATFORM-001 built ExitOutcome::Stalled and Command::With_Idle_Timeout precisely so a stalled process could be told apart from one legitimately taking a long time, and named wiring a real default into the ledger's own predicate execution as a decision left to whichever item takes it up. crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/finish/running.rs's Commanded builds every Command through Command::New alone and never calls With_Idle_Timeout, so idle_timeout always equals timeout: a real predicate that hangs silently is reported as the same TimedOut a predicate that ran the full wall bound producing output would be, which is exactly the ambiguity the memory nomos-shell-and-gate-traps and this workspace's own Runner comment describe as costly to diagnose.
items.done_when: crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/finish/running.rs's Commanded (or Runner) threads an idle bound shorter than the wall timeout into every Command it builds for Finish's gate step and predicate run, using Command::With_Idle_Timeout. The chosen default and the reasoning for its value are stated in a doc comment beside the change. A test proves the property end to end: a fake launcher or a real child process that stops producing output well before the wall timeout elapses is reported through Finish as an idle-triggered Stalled outcome (FinishRefusal::NoVerdict carrying ExitOutcome::Stalled) rather than only ever reaching TimedOut at the wall bound. Existing Finish tests continue to pass unchanged in the case where a predicate keeps producing output or exits promptly.

items.title: Component::All is a declared universe with no mirror, and D-134 prices exactly this gap
items.why: D-134's own consequences section says an unmirrored universe 'makes each one a line of output with a named risk instead of a silence' rather than closing it outright, and tests/contract/tests/completeness_universes/table.rs already classifies crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/src/component.rs's Component::All (9 variants) as Standing::Unmirrored with a stated risk ('a component added without adding it here is left out of fact identity, and OD-ANALYSIS-001 makes that a reuse defect'). Component is a closed enum, so its reality is a compile-time property: an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm is a real mirror in D-134's sense (compares the declaration against what it claims to enumerate), the same shape crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/item/tests.rs already uses for a similar enum, and RowKind::Label's own match at crates/spec/nomos-spec-model/src/table/row_kind.rs is already exhaustive without a wildcard as a working local precedent for the pattern.
items.done_when: component.rs declares its mirror at the site in a doc comment above Component::All (the 'Mirrored by TestName' idiom D-134 established, e.g. as seen above DECLARED_RULES in crates/spec/nomos-spec-validate/src/run.rs). A real test (in component.rs itself as a unit test, or in crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/tests/fact_identity/key_identity.rs alongside the file's existing Component::All usages -- whichever fits the crate's existing test organization) exhaustively matches every Component variant with no wildcard arm, so the test fails to compile if a variant is added to the enum without being added to the match. tests/contract/tests/completeness_universes/table.rs's Component::All row changes from Standing::Unmirrored to Standing::Mirrored { by: "<the new test's name>" } and UNMIRRORED_TOTAL is decremented from 13 to 12 to match. cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests --test completeness_universes and cargo test -p nomos-analysis both pass; nomos check no longer reports Component::All as an advisory finding.

items.title: nomos-check-orchestration hand-calls one rule and hand-declares one capability, and nothing decides what the second one does to Run()
items.why: run.rs::Run() hand-calls Check_Completeness_Mirrors by name and composition.rs::Registered() hand-declares exactly one capability contract against exactly one provider offer -- correct at nomos-rules' current size, its first and only shipped rule, but nothing on the board or in a governing record decides what adding a second rule or a second capability/provider pair does to either function. Two shapes are both plausible from here: Run() could gain a declared rule-selection mechanism driven by what a request asks for, or it could grow a second hand-written call beside the first, then a third, deciding the seam by accretion rather than by a recorded choice. OD-HOST-002 already treats this crate's composition as reconstructable state and names the registry-rendered-twice duplication in tests/integration/src/context.rs without settling this question, which is a different one: not whether the state is privileged, but whether the composition mechanism itself scales past one entry by design or by habit. ARC-HARNESS-001 and D-135 are the precedent for deciding a seam like this before code accretes across it rather than after.
items.done_when: A new record under OD-HOST decides, for nomos-check-orchestration's Registered() and Run(), whether a second rule or a second capability/provider pair must be admitted through a declared selection mechanism -- the rule or provider a request needs, resolved from a declaration rather than named in the function body -- or whether hand-written composition remains correct at that size too, and states the concrete criterion, for example a count or a property of the second entry, that would flip the answer, so the choice is checkable rather than re-argued when nomos-rules ships its second rule. items.title: OD-STORE-002 worked-case query becomes a report, not a gate
items.why: OD-STORE-002 Worked Case names a join: does a crates tests/contract/surface/C.txt blob differ between a commit ranges endpoints, and does any commit in that range touch docs/records/. No code anywhere in this workspace shells to git; the two committed series sit unqueried next to each other. Two checks before building this: first, the same record own What A Temporal Claim Is Evidence Of section says a temporal or cross-revision claim must never gate the change that produced the observation it depends on, so the output has to be a report a human reads, never a cargo test wired into the gate workflow or into any crates default test suite -- P3-REGRESSION already established the report-not-gate shape for a cross-revision finding in this workspace. Second, a measured false-positive class already exists: of 59 commits touching tests/contract/surface/ across this repository history, 21 (36 percent) touch zero paths under docs/records/ in that same commit, including 27b3ed9 which reblessed a stale mirror with no accompanying decision to record. The join read literally over single-commit ranges is genuinely noisy, but the record leaves the choice of range to the caller rather than deciding a default, and OD-STORE-002 already classifies this whole class of finding as EvidenceClass Derived, read alongside a live check and never substituted for one -- so a human choosing the range and reading the findings, rather than the tool inferring record-worthiness itself, is exactly the reading the record already commits to. Nothing about the join itself needs a fresh design decision; only its delivery as an always-passing, explicitly-invoked report does.
items.done_when: A new bin-only crate nomos-surface-provenance (crates/host/nomos-surface-provenance, band 91, no src/lib.rs, matching nomos-cli shape) implements OD-STORE-002 Worked Case query exactly, for a caller-given pair of git revisions --since and --until and a crate name with a tests/contract/surface/<crate>.txt snapshot: whether the blob at that path differs between the two revisions (git diff <since> <until> --name-only -- tests/contract/surface/<crate>.txt, nonempty means yes) and whether any commit in <since>..<until> touches docs/records/ (git log <since>..<until> --format=%H -- docs/records/, nonempty means yes). A finding is reported exactly when the first is yes and the second is no. With no --crate flag every crate holding a tests/contract/surface/<name>.txt file is checked, names discovered from that directory filenames; one or more --crate <name> flags narrow the set. Findings render to stdout naming the crate and the commits that touched its surface file in range, so a reader can judge each one -- including a reblessing-only change like 27b3ed9 -- without the tool asserting a verdict about record-worthiness itself. The two git invocations run through nomos_platform ProcessLauncher (nomos_platform_std StdProcessLauncher wired in main.rs), so the join logic itself is unit-tested (cargo test -p nomos-surface-provenance) against a fake launcher returning fixed argv-matched output, never against this repository own real git history, whose completeness the gate workflow does not guarantee (actions/checkout there sets no fetch-depth, so a CI checkout may be shallow). The binary exits 0 whenever it ran a query to completion, whether or not a finding was reported, and a non-zero code only for a usage error (missing --since or --until) or a launcher failure -- a finding existing may never produce a non-zero exit. Nothing in the gate workflow, the root Cargo.toml build, or any other crate test suite invokes this binary; it is run by a human on demand. The crate joins the workspace members list in Cargo.toml (under the Band 10 -- host comment, beside nomos-cli), README band table at band 91 with a one-line description, and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs BANDS at the same band and description; tests/contract/tests/public_surface/snapshots.rs WITHOUT_A_LIBRARY gains nomos-surface-provenance beside nomos-cli, since it has no library target. tests/contract/tests/boundaries/readme.rs, graph.rs and reachability.rs pass unmodified against the new crate.

items.title: OD-SPEC-004's filler test becomes the repetition census it already recommends, or admits it isn't a preservation guarantee
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 measured a quantified, undeclared miss: the governed wording template hollows 132 v15.0 documents and 44 restored members, none of it caught because the live filler test is blocklist substring matching alone. The record itself lists three closing options and recommends option 1 -- a repetition census with the blocklist retained as the naming layer -- and says nothing is blocked on adopting it, since the archaeology module's regression-report tooling (crates/spec/nomos-spec-ingest/src/archaeology/census.rs) already implements exactly that shape for cross-revision reporting: Shared_Templates groups by repeated body text at or above SHARED_BY (3) sections and Is_Filler supplies the declared/undeclared label. Nothing turns that recommendation into the ruleset nomos-spec-validate actually enforces: NSV-PRESERVE-004 is discussed only in this record's own prose, absent from both DECLARED_RULES (crates/spec/nomos-spec-validate/src/run.rs) and Registered() (crates/spec/nomos-spec-validate/src/preserve.rs), which today only claim NSV-PRESERVE-001/002/003/006. That is the crate correctly refusing to claim a rule nobody decided the shape of, per OD-COMPLETENESS-002 -- not an oversight -- so closing it requires making the decision the record already leans toward, not silently adding a rule.
items.done_when: docs/records/OD-SPEC-004-the-filler-blocklist-misses-the-wording-that-hollowed-v15.md gains a top-level '## Resolution' section adopting option 1 exactly as its own '## What Would Close It' section recommends (a repetition census with the blocklist retained as the naming layer), and its frontmatter status changes from open to accepted. crates/spec/nomos-spec-validate/src/rule/ gains a new rule file implementing the Rule trait with Id() returning "NSV-PRESERVE-004" and Describe() naming the check; its Evaluate(&self, store: &SpecificationStore) groups source_blocks rows by normalized_hash, counts DISTINCT document_uid per group, treats a group whose distinct-document count is at or above nomos_spec_ingest::SHARED_BY (3) as a template, and reports a violation for a template whose text nomos_spec_ingest::Is_Filler returns None for (the undeclared case) -- one violation per undeclared template, naming the section/document count it spans, never one per row. A template Is_Filler already matches is not a violation: the blocklist stays the naming layer, not a second gate. NSV-PRESERVE-004 is added to DECLARED_RULES in run.rs and to the Vec returned by Registered() in preserve.rs, beside the existing four. nomos-spec-validate's Cargo.toml moves nomos-spec-ingest from [dev-dependencies] to [dependencies] (band 13 before band 14 already permits this), since the new rule reuses Is_Filler and SHARED_BY rather than redefining them. A unit test proves the rule flags only the undeclared case: an in-memory SpecificationStore seeded with >=3 blocks sharing a normalized_hash whose text Is_Filler does not match reports one violation, and a second fixture whose shared text Is_Filler does match reports none. cargo test -p nomos-spec-validate -p nomos-spec-ingest passes, and the existing registry-vs-manifest reconciliation in run.rs still holds with five declared rules instead of four. diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md (plus their .nomos-projection.json sidecars) are re-rendered from a worktree holding exactly the record set this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005, and nomos spec freshness --into . --require diagram-set --require domain-specification exits 0 in that worktree.

Declined.reason: done_when misstated the SHARED_BY threshold as distinct-document count instead of section (row) count, which the record and archaeology/census.rs both use. Superseded by P13-NSV-PRESERVE-004-2 with the corrected threshold.

abandoned.reason: done_when misstated the SHARED_BY threshold as distinct-document count; the record and archaeology/census.rs both define it as section (row) count. Re-adding corrected.

items.title: Two universes sharing a bare name in different crates share one SubjectId, the qualified-name fix D-134 named and left unwritten
items.why: D-134's own text says: 'Two universes sharing a name in different crates would share a subject identity. Nothing in this workspace does today. The fix is a qualified name, not a path, and it is not written yet.' crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/mirror/verdict.rs's Judge/Shortcoming builds a completeness-mirror Finding's subject as SubjectId::From_Digest(Content_Digest(universe.name.as_bytes())) -- the bare DeclaredUniverse.name only, with no crate qualifier -- so two universes named identically in different crates (e.g. two enums both ending in ::All whose owning type shares a name, or two identically-named constants) would hash to the same SubjectId and be indistinguishable in nomos check's findings, suppressions, or any history keyed on subject. Confirmed this is still live: DeclaredUniverse.path is documented 'for reporting; never identity' and DeclaredUniverse.name is documented 'the stable name... A universe that moves file keeps it' -- so the fix per D-134's own words is a qualified name (a stable crate/suite qualifier prepended to name), not the raw path, which is why locations already carries universe.path separately for reporting and must stay untouched. The existing completeness_universes/table.rs comparisons (claims.rs, derivation.rs) already key on (path, name) tuples and are unaffected -- this item is contained to subject construction, not the declared-universe scan or table.rs.
items.done_when: crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/mirror/verdict.rs's Shortcoming (or a new helper beside it) derives a stable qualifier from universe.path -- the crate or test-suite directory the path names (e.g. crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/src/table.rs yields nomos-spec-store, tests/contract/src/gates.rs yields nomos-contract-tests), by splitting the path on its /src/ or /tests/ segment and taking the leaf directory name before it, not by reading Cargo.toml or the filesystem (this rule stays a pure function over the syntax facts it is handed). SubjectId::From_Digest is built from Content_Digest of the qualified string (qualifier + universe.name, e.g. "nomos-spec-store::Table::All"), not universe.name alone. subject_name and locations are unchanged (still universe.name and universe.path respectively), since D-134 only names subject identity as the gap, not reporting. A unit test in nomos-rules proves two DeclaredUniverse values with the same name and different path (in different crate directories) now produce different SubjectId values, where they previously collided. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-rules passes, and the existing nomos-rules and nomos-contract-tests completeness_universes suites are unaffected (their comparisons key on (path, name), not on SubjectId).

items.title: Validate never refuses a hand-edited territory carrying a pattern, the completeness gap OD-LEDGER-013 named and left open
items.why: OD-LEDGER-013 withdrew work add --territory-pattern as a usage error but deliberately kept Territory::patterns and its Unknown-intersection semantics, because a hand-edited or future-authoring-surface-written document could still arrive carrying one and must fail closed rather than compare as touching nothing. The record's own text: 'Refuse patterns in Validate, so the document rejects one too. This is the more complete answer... It is not done here because Validate lives in store.rs, which is outside P10-PATTERN-BRICK's territory... this is a completeness gap and not a hole. It is worth an item.' Confirmed still true: crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store/validation.rs's Check_Territory checks Ambiguous_Paths() and empty territory, but never inspects item.territory.patterns -- a hand-edited ledger document with a non-empty patterns array on a workable item passes validate today. The design itself is already fully settled by OD-LEDGER-013 (keep the field, keep Unknown semantics for existing comparisons, work add stays refusing the flag) -- this item only adds the one missing Check_* function validation.rs's own existing pattern already follows for every other rule (Check_Dependencies, Check_State, Check_Predicate).
items.done_when: validation.rs gains a new Check_Pattern (or folded into Check_Territory) that reports a violation for any item whose territory.patterns is non-empty, naming the item id and the pattern, in the same style the other Check_* functions use (format!, pushed to violations). A unit test in validation.rs's own test module (or a sibling tests file, matching the existing convention in that crate) constructs a LedgerItem with a non-empty territory.patterns and asserts Validate reports it. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-ledger passes, including the existing test fixtures that legitimately carry "patterns": [] (empty) which must keep passing unaffected.

Declined.reason: superseded by P13-VALIDATE-PATTERN-REFUSAL-2: same fix, corrected territory (adds the shared test-helper files under tests/exclusion_holds/) and a predicate scoped to --test exclusion_holds instead of the whole crate, to avoid an unrelated pre-existing failure in records_do_not_serialize.

abandoned.reason: territory only reserved crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store/validation.rs, but the correct implementation needed shared test-helper additions across tests/exclusion_holds/{board,claiming,validation}.rs too; also the item's predicate (cargo test -p nomos-ledger) pulls in an unrelated pre-existing failing suite, records_do_not_serialize, confirmed via git stash A/B unrelated to this change. Abandoning to re-author -2 with corrected territory and a predicate scoped to the test binary the new tests actually live in.

items.title: kind and origin print only via work show, never work list or work audit, the display gap OD-LEDGER-024 named as follow-on
items.why: OD-LEDGER-024 gave every ledger item a closed kind and origin field and said: 'It does not add ordering over kind or origin to work list or work audit beyond what work show now prints. A reader wanting to prioritize Decision work over Cleanup work today still reads show per item; building that into a listing is follow-on, not this record's done_when.' Confirmed still true: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs prints kind/origin in work show's per-item detail; crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/listing.rs (work list's Print_Listing) and crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs (work audit) print neither field anywhere in their per-item output. This is explicitly scoped by the record as display only -- not the ordering/ranking question OD-LEDGER-017's deferred priority field and OD-LEDGER-022/024's scheduler-classification gap are about, which stay out of this item's scope entirely.
items.done_when: work list's per-item line (Print_Listing in listing.rs) and work audit's per-item report (report.rs) each print the item's kind and origin alongside what they already print, in a format consistent with each command's existing column/line style (read both files' current output shape before choosing the exact placement -- do not redesign either command's layout beyond adding these two fields). No new sorting, filtering, or ranking behavior is added -- items still print in whatever order each command already uses. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-cli passes, including any existing snapshot/golden-output tests for work list or work audit, which must be updated to include the new fields if they assert exact output text.

items.title: nomos-lang-package's language-agnostic core moves to its own crate, so a second language never depends on Rust to read its own manifest
items.why: Investigating what a second (non-Rust) language provider would need to reuse for its own package manifest found nomos-lang-package is not generic despite its name: Cargo.toml names nomos-lang-rust and nomos-lang-rust-scan as direct dependencies, KNOWN_PROVIDERS pulls their PROVIDER constants directly, and RustEdition is a closed four-variant Rust-edition enum the reader resolves language_versions against by name. A second language's package crate could not depend on this crate without also depending on Rust's two providers. PackageVersion, ProtocolRange, ProviderRegistration and ManifestError, by contrast, are already fully language-agnostic on inspection -- none names Rust or imports a provider crate. OD-PACKAGE-007 records the split this finding motivates.
items.done_when: A new crate crates/packages/nomos-package (band 24) carries PackageVersion, ProtocolRange, ProviderRegistration and ManifestError (moved verbatim) plus a PackageManifest type with language_versions: Vec<String> (raw labels, no typed version-domain abstraction invented) and providers: Vec<ProviderRegistration>. Its Parse_Manifest(text, at, known_providers: &[&str]) and Read_Manifest(path, known_providers: &[&str]) take the provider allowlist as a parameter and depend on nothing above nomos-contracts/serde/serde_json. nomos-lang-package keeps its exact existing public surface unchanged -- Parse_Manifest(text, at) and Read_Manifest(path) keep their current signatures, LanguagePackage keeps language_versions: Vec<RustEdition>, RustEdition/KNOWN_PROVIDERS/Is_Known stay where they are -- calling into nomos-package internally and resolving RustEdition itself, reusing (not redefining) PackageVersion/ProtocolRange/ProviderRegistration/ManifestError via re-export. crates/packages/nomos-lang-package/tests/manifest.rs passes unchanged, byte for byte, as the behavior-preservation proof. Cargo.toml (workspace members and [workspace.dependencies]), README.md and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs gain nomos-package's band-24 row; tests/contract/surface gains nomos-package's snapshot and nomos-lang-package's is reblessed if its rendering changes. nomos-package's own test suite exercises Parse_Manifest/Read_Manifest with a known_providers list of its own (not Rust's), proving the split works for a provider set other than the one it was extracted from.

items.why: OD-HOST-004 decided nomos_check_orchestration::run::Run stays hand-written for as long as every rule it calls runs unconditionally, and named the flip criterion as conditionality, not cardinality: Run needs a declared selection mechanism the moment a rule's participation is meant to vary by request rather than by whether the crate merely knows about it. crates/rules/nomos-rules holds exactly one rule today and has no package or registration contract of its own -- unlike the capability side, which already separated nomos-cap-syntax from its first provider so a second provider could offer against a contract that was never any one provider's property. items.title: nomos-rules gains a second rule, Check_Naming_Convention, judging Pascal_Snake_Case function names
items.why: Explicit direction to invest in a second, genuinely useful rule -- both to prove the RuleRegistry contract P13-RULE-REGISTRY-BASE-3 built against a real second party, and to give OD-PACKAGE-008's question (whether a future RulePackage manifest's field boundaries generalize past a population of one rule) a second data point to reason from. README.md's Conventions section states directly that function names are Pascal_Snake_Case, and Cargo.toml's own [workspace.lints.rust] comment names the resulting gap: non_snake_case is set to allow specifically because of this convention, and nothing was turned on to check the convention that replaced it. This rule reads the same nomos.cap.syntax.items facts Check_Completeness_Mirrors already reads (no new capability contract needed) and reconciles each function's own name against the workspace's stated convention -- a one-sided lexical predicate, deliberately different in shape from the mirror rule's two-sided claim-vs-fact reconciliation, so it is a real second data point and not a copy of the first rule's own shape.
items.done_when: crates/rules/nomos-rules exposes Check_Naming_Convention(sources, facts) -> Vec<Finding> and NAMING_CONVENTION, matching Check_Completeness_Mirrors's existing signature shape. It judges every Function item nomos.cap.syntax.items facts declare: Own_Name() must be Pascal_Snake_Case (each underscore-separated segment starts uppercase-ASCII or is all-digits), exempting the literal main and any function enclosed by a trait implementation (name fixed by the trait, not by this workspace). A subject whose fact cannot be read produces a finding rather than rendering as clean, matching the mirror rule's own principle. Findings report GateCategory::Advisory (a newly-added, not-yet-broadly-verified check, deliberately not Blocking on its first landing) and EvidenceClass::Derived. Not wired into crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/run.rs::Run -- that is a separate decision OD-HOST-004 already governs, and this item does not make nomos check report it. Not registered into RuleRegistry either -- OD-RULES-004 states that registration is optional for the registry's first real consumer. tests/contract/surface/nomos-rules.txt is reblessed for the new exports (NOMOS_SURFACE_BLESS=nomos-rules cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests --test public_surface). cargo test -p nomos-rules -p nomos-contract-tests passes, and the rule has been sanity-checked against real source files in this repository (not only hand-written fixtures) before landing, with the check script removed before commit.

items.title: Whether RuleOffer needs a measured Inputs classification now, or waits for a caching consumer
items.why: code-standards/nomos-proto (github.com/kevinmettias/nomos-proto), an earlier Go implementation of the same tool this workspace rebuilds in Rust, declares a closed, optional checkspec.Inputs enum (INPUT_SCOPED_FILES, INPUT_WHOLE_CORPUS, INPUT_REPOSITORY_CONFIG, INPUT_EXTERNAL_TOOL) on every check -- stated by the rule itself, defaulting to undeclared (which disables caching rather than wrongly enabling it), and explicitly measured rather than typed from reading the source, because a plausible-but-unmeasured list would be indistinguishable from a measured one while carrying none of the evidence. nomos-rules' new registration contract (crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/registry.rs, from OD-RULES-004 / P13-RULE-REGISTRY-BASE-3) carries RuleOffer{rule, contract_record, contract_record_version} with no equivalent: a rule states which capability contract it reads through Syntax_Requirement, but nothing states what kind of input its answer depends on. nomos-analysis already treats invalidation as a first-class fact-layer concern (crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/src/invalidation.rs) that a rule-level classification would extend rather than introduce from nothing. The registry's own module doc states plainly that nothing in nomos_check_orchestration::run::Run consults it yet, so there is no identified consumer today -- the open question is whether that absence means the classification belongs in RuleOffer now, before nomos-rules' two rules and any future rule package multiply the migration cost, or whether it should wait for an actual caching/invalidation consumer to exist first, the same population-of-two caution OD-PACKAGE-006 originally stated for KNOWN_PROVIDERS before this workspace's own explicit direction to build language/rule plugin infrastructure ahead of demonstrated need overrode it there.
items.done_when: A new record under OD-RULES states, for nomos-rules' RuleOffer: whether it gains a closed, optional Inputs-shaped classification now (naming a rule's dependency as roughly per-file, whole-corpus, repository-configuration, or external-tool, defaulting to undeclared/conservative, measured rather than guessed) or waits for a real caching/invalidation consumer in nomos_check_orchestration or nomos-analysis to exist first. It cites code-standards/nomos-proto's checkspec.Inputs as the precedent and states the concrete trigger that would flip the answer if it declines to build now. It relates to OD-RULES-004, D-135 and nomos-analysis's existing invalidation module, is registered in crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/, and diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are re-rendered and current per nomos spec freshness, verified from an isolated worktree at the record set this commit publishes. Closed by the record alone: no crate changes, and nomos-rules is not touched.

items.title: Whether a provider needs a declared decline-with-reason, or waits for a second capability contract
items.why: code-standards/nomos-proto (github.com/kevinmettias/nomos-proto), an earlier Go implementation of the same tool this workspace rebuilds in Rust, gives every language kernel a <lang>_declines.go pattern -- DeclinedCapabilities.Declined_Capability(capability) -> (reason, declined) -- letting a provider state, ahead of time and in one discoverable place, that it will never offer against a capability, and why. Its own decline map runs to roughly seventy reasoned entries in production. crates/substrate/nomos-capability/src/provider_offer.rs's ProviderOffer{provider, capability, version, guarantee} has no equivalent, and offer_refusal.rs's OfferRefusal is a different concept entirely -- why the registry rejects a bad submission (ForUndeclared/ExceedsCeiling/Duplicate), not a provider's own advance statement that it will never offer. Today a provider that does not offer against a capability is indistinguishable from one that was never asked, and only one capability contract exists in this workspace (nomos.cap.syntax.items, crates/capabilities/nomos-cap-syntax), so there is no second contract for a real provider to structurally decline against yet -- the same population-of-two shape OD-PACKAGE-006 originally deferred for KNOWN_PROVIDERS and OD-RULES-005 left open for RuleOffer's Inputs classification.

items.title: OD-PACKAGE-008 gains code-standards' own per-check packaging abandonment as corroborating evidence
items.why: A fuller research pass over code-standards/nomos-proto's rule/check architecture (this session, 2026-08-18) found direct, verifiable evidence bearing on OD-PACKAGE-008's open question. That Go system's own go.work carries this comment verbatim: 'This file carried 45 entries -- one per check -- because every check was its own Go module. That boundary was packaging, never design: it forced the gate to go run each check, and it is why a shared driver could not simply be imported.' A mature, production system directly analogous to nomos-rules tried independently packaging each rule/check as its own unit and reversed it, for a concrete technical reason (a shared driver could not be imported across module boundaries) rather than merely a population-of-one caution. OD-PACKAGE-008 currently reasons about the RulePackage manifest question from first principles alone (population of one rule, ARCH-002's contents list) with no external corroborating case. This is exactly the shape of evidence OD-RULES-004 already cites nomos-add-plugin section 2 for and OD-RULES-005 already cites nomos-proto's checkspec.Inputs for -- verified directly against the Go repo's own go.work file, not secondhand.
items.done_when: OD-PACKAGE-008's version is bumped and a new subsection (e.g. under Current Position or a new Corroborating Evidence heading) quotes go.work's comment verbatim, states which repository and file it is from, and states plainly what it does and does not prove: that per-artifact packaging at a population comparable to nomos-rules' today was tried by a mature analogous system and reversed for a driver-composition reason, not proof that nomos-rules' own eventual second rule will diverge the same way. The record's Status and open question are unchanged -- this is a citation added to an open record, not a resolution. items.title: nomos-analysis's dirty-propagation walk is fused with fact-identity vocabulary, contrary to D-135/D-138's rename-later contract
items.why: D-135 sends domain-neutral code (no crate/rule/finding/claim vocabulary) to XVPE authorship by default; D-138 says where XVPE cannot yet absorb it, Nomos builds it under an ordinary crate name whose public contract still carries no Nomos-specific vocabulary, so a later rename-and-move is mechanical. MemoryFactStore (crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/src/fact/memory_store.rs) implements exactly the kind of mechanism D-130's own rationale names as an XVPE candidate -- dirty propagation and topological layering over a dependents adjacency map keyed on opaque Digest128 -- but its propagation walk (Invalidate_Named/Follow_Edges/Reach/Spreading) is not separated from Component/FactKey/GenerationCause, which are Nomos-specific fact-identity vocabulary. A later extraction is a rewrite, not a rename, contradicting D-138's own stated cost claim.
items.done_when: The dependents/keys adjacency walk (Invalidate_Named, Follow_Edges, Reach, Spreading, Opened, Settle, Note_Broadening's non-Nomos parts) is isolated in a module whose types reference only opaque digests and generic dependency edges -- no FactIdentity, FactKey, Component, GenerationCause, or other fact-identity vocabulary in its own signatures -- with MemoryFactStore adapting it for the FactStore contract. cargo test -p nomos-analysis passes with unchanged externally-observable behavior (same test assertions), and a test asserts the new module's source contains no  of the fact-identity types.

items.title: nomos-analysis dirty-propagation walk is fused with fact-identity vocabulary, contrary to D-135/D-138 rename-later contract
items.why: D-135 sends domain-neutral code (no crate, rule, finding, or claim vocabulary) to XVPE authorship by default; D-138 says where XVPE cannot yet absorb it, Nomos builds it under an ordinary crate name whose public contract still carries no Nomos-specific vocabulary, so a later rename-and-move is mechanical. MemoryFactStore (crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/src/fact/memory_store.rs) implements exactly the kind of mechanism D-130's own rationale names as an XVPE candidate: dirty propagation and topological layering over a dependents adjacency map keyed on opaque Digest128. Its propagation walk, Invalidate_Named, Follow_Edges, Reach and Spreading, is not separated from Component, FactKey and GenerationCause, which are Nomos-specific fact-identity vocabulary. A later extraction is a rewrite, not a rename, contradicting D-138's own stated cost claim.
items.done_when: The dependents and keys adjacency walk, Invalidate_Named, Follow_Edges, Reach, Spreading, Opened, Settle, and the non-Nomos parts of Note_Broadening, is isolated in a module whose types reference only opaque digests and generic dependency edges, with no FactIdentity, FactKey, Component, or GenerationCause in its own signatures, and MemoryFactStore adapts it for the FactStore contract. cargo test -p nomos-analysis passes with unchanged externally observable behavior, and a test asserts the new module imports none of the fact-identity types.

items.title: Whether the provider convention needs a declared trait, or waits for a third provider
items.why: Three research memos comparing nomos against its Go-era predecessor nomos-proto/code-standards were reviewed this session. The highest-ranked recommendation in one of them is to formalize the provider convention -- the PROVIDER constant, Declared_Guarantee(), and Materialize() every capability provider implements -- as a real Rust trait rather than a bare naming convention. The memo's motivating case: a check-local Go package once hand-rolled its own copy of the Rust language type; Go's structural typing let it silently satisfy less than the real interface, and the resolver fell back to a weaker default with no build error -- fixed only by hand-added var _ Interface = Type{} compile-time assertions. crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/src/provider.rs and crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-scan/src/provider.rs both hand-implement the identical four-part shape today (PROVIDER, Declared_Guarantee, Materialize, and an identically-shaped FactContext) with no shared trait -- two real, live implementations exist, so a trait would not be designed from zero instances. But composition.rs already calls each provider's function by its real, statically-resolved name (registry.Offer(nomos_lang_rust::Provider_Offer())), which has no structural-typing hole for a trait to close the way Go's did -- and both provider.rs files carry doc comments explicitly defending deliberate duplication elsewhere in the same files (Encode_Payload), a design tension a trait proposal should not gloss over.
items.done_when: A new record under OD-CAPABILITY states whether PROVIDER/Declared_Guarantee/Materialize gains a declared trait now, before a third provider multiplies the migration cost, or waits for one to exist so the design has a real case to check against -- and states plainly why Rust's static call-site checking already closes the specific structural-typing hole the Go bug exploited, so the record is not framed as fixing an active bug. It follows OD-CAPABILITY-007's shape (Question / Current Position / What Would Decide It / Status), relates to OD-CAPABILITY-001, OD-CAPABILITY-007 and OD-PACKAGE-006, and states the concrete trigger that would flip the answer (a third provider, or a consumer needing to hold providers polymorphically). Registered in crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/, and diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md (with sidecars) are re-rendered and fresh per nomos spec freshness --require diagram-set --require domain-specification, verified from an isolated worktree holding exactly the record set this commit publishes. Closed by the record alone: no crate changes.

items.title: propagation::Spread is a bare function, not a substitution seam; nothing proves an alternate implementation can replace it
items.why: P13-ANALYSIS-PROPAGATION-SEAM-2 separated the dirty-propagation walk into propagation.rs, free of fact-identity vocabulary, but left it a plain function MemoryFactStore calls directly. That satisfies D-135/D-138's vocabulary requirement but not the actual migration promise: nothing demonstrates the mechanism is swappable without touching FactStore or its consumers, which is the property D-130's deferred-adoption design is supposed to buy. FactStore itself stays sealed and untouched; this item is only about the internal seam beneath it, per the reviewed correction that the replaceable boundary belongs below FactStore, not at it.
items.done_when: propagation.rs declares a crate-private DependencyPropagation trait with exactly one method matching todays Spread signature, plus the one implementation MemoryFactStore actually uses today. MemoryFactStore gains a crate-private constructor that accepts a boxed DependencyPropagation implementation, with its existing public New() defaulting to the current implementation so FactStore consumers and its public API are unchanged. A test constructs a MemoryFactStore with a second, distinct DependencyPropagation implementation (not just the default) and shows FactStore::Invalidate produces the same InvalidationReport shape as the default implementation over the same fixture, proving substitution does not require touching FactStore or its consumers. A second test extends the existing vocabulary conformance check to also forbid Broadening, Supersession and GuaranteeDigest in propagation.rs's non-comment, non-test code, as a negative control against provider-broadening or supersession policy migrating into the generic mechanism merely because it participates in invalidation. cargo test -p nomos-analysis passes with the pre-existing 36 tests unchanged in behavior. No XVPE dependency is introduced anywhere in the workspace.

items.title: The manifest JSON gains a required schema_version, refusing what this build cannot read
items.why: A real manifest file already exists on disk (packages/nomos.lang.rust.json) with a real consumer (nomos_lang_package::Read_Manifest) and no marker anywhere saying which revision of the JSON field layout it was written against. code-standards/nomos-proto's own out-of-process plugin manifest carries a third, independent MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION for exactly this (verified directly against kernel/plugin/installation_contract.go), and this workspace already has its own closer precedent for the identical problem: nomos-ledger's LedgerDocument.schema_version, checked against SCHEMA_VERSION before a document is trusted (crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store/document.rs, store.rs), specifically so a newer-schema file is refused with a legible reason rather than misread as merely malformed. Unlike this session's other two corpus-inspired questions (OD-CAPABILITY-007 decline-with-reason, OD-RULES-006 EnforcementPlacementRationale), this has a real, live consumer and a real, already-published artifact today, and nomos's own ledger schema field is direct internal precedent that the design already works for this exact class of problem -- not machinery designed against zero instances.
items.done_when: nomos_package::Parse_Manifest reads a required schema_version field first, refusing ManifestError::MissingField if absent (the existing variant, no new one needed there) and a new ManifestError::UnknownSchema{at,understood,found} if the manifest names a schema newer than this build's SCHEMA_VERSION constant (starting at 1, pub, mirroring nomos-ledger::store::SCHEMA_VERSION). PackageManifest's parsed shape and every other refusal are unchanged. crates/packages/nomos-package/tests/manifest.rs and crates/packages/nomos-lang-package/tests/manifest.rs's fixtures carry schema_version, plus a new test exercising UnknownSchema. packages/nomos.lang.rust.json, the one real manifest on disk, carries schema_version: 1. tests/contract/surface/nomos-package.txt is reblessed for the new ManifestError variant and the new SCHEMA_VERSION export. A new record under OD-PACKAGE (accepted, not open -- a real consumer and real precedent decide this rather than defer it) states the decision, cites nomos-ledger's own schema_version as precedent and code-standards' MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION as convergent prior art, verified directly against both. Registered in crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/, diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md (with sidecars) re-rendered and fresh per nomos spec freshness --require diagram-set --require domain-specification from an isolated worktree holding exactly the record set this commit publishes.

items.title: OD-LEDGER-001's changeset-model/rule-engine gate is not actually clear yet
items.why: OD-LEDGER-001 says nomos.rules.work-ledger closes it and names two prerequisites -- the changeset model and the rule engine -- as why it 'cannot be built earlier'. Both types now nominally exist (nomos_workspace::WorkspaceChangeSet, and nomos-rules with two real rules), which reads as the gate having cleared. Direct investigation shows it has not: the only real (non-test) WorkspaceChangeSet producer, As_One_Checkout in nomos-check-orchestration/src/facts.rs, wraps a full-tree snapshot of the current disk, not a diff of what a claim holder actually committed -- there is no producer that builds a changeset from git history at all. LedgerItem records no commit SHA or range for a claim (only a single post-hoc verified.revision was just added by OD-LEDGER-027), so 'the set of paths a holder modified' cannot even be asked for yet. OD-LEDGER-027 itself deliberately left subprocess git integration and any territory-scoped diff to a later item with a different question -- this is that item. Separately, every existing nomos-rules rule has the signature fn(sources: &[SourceFile], facts: &mut dyn FactReader) -> Vec<Finding>, a subject shape built for judging source text, not a changeset-vs-territory comparison; nomos.rules.work-ledger would not fit the convention nomos-add-plugin documents without either bending it or being a different kind of check entirely. Authoring nomos.rules.work-ledger as a ledger item today would very likely repeat the exact failure OD-LEDGER-001 is about: an item whose territory names nomos-rules but whose real work lands in nomos-ledger's schema and a new git-reading module nobody named.
items.done_when: OD-LEDGER-001 is amended (version 5) to state precisely, with current evidence, what remains before nomos.rules.work-ledger is buildable: (1) a per-claim commit-range or start-SHA field the ledger schema does not carry today, (2) a real changeset producer built from git history rather than a full-tree snapshot, and (3) that the existing nomos-rules rule signature (sources + FactReader) does not fit this rule's subject and either needs a documented exception or a different composition seam. The amendment does not build any of the three -- it corrects 'What Would Close It' from a two-item list that reads as satisfied to an accurate one that is not, the same kind of premise-correction P13-D130-REVERIFY already made for D-130. domain-specification.md (and diagram-set if relations changed) are re-rendered and fresh, from an isolated worktree holding exactly this commit's record set.

items.title: Determine and record the near-term implementation boundary for production Nomos Core, before architecture/feature intelligence and rich clients
items.why: Two sessions of external architecture review, subagent verification against current HEAD, and a structural survey of the 363-requirement v14 corpus (61 families, read directly from NOMOS_V14_CORPUS's requirements directory) converged independently on the same two-tier split: a headless enforcement core (kernel/identity, analysis+invalidation substrate, language/provider/capability, rules, applicability+coverage, gates, baselines/suppressions/adoption, corrections, workflow orchestration, application-service boundary, CLI/API/MCP projections, model-backend/agent-executor infrastructure, production hardening) versus deferred consuming systems (architecture discovery, feature topology/path tracing, placement analysis, runtime/debug/test intelligence, Atlas, desktop/web/mobile). items.title: ARC-ROADMAP-001's first-class Gate object gets its crate, starting with Plan over the rule registry
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names a first-class Gate object as near-term work, distinct from OD-GATE-004's CI step: "a first-class object an end-user repository would configure (ScopeSelector, RuleSelector, ApplicabilityPolicy, CoveragePolicy, BaselinePolicy, SuppressionPolicy, required phases, evidence requirements, failure disposition), exposed as nomos gate plan / run / explain / compare". WF-001 (v14 corpus, volume-05.7-4-gates-phases-and-workflows, canonical-normative-record) makes it binding: "A gate shall define policy: required phases, thresholds, coverage, unsupported-analysis policy, waivers, approvals, and blocking behavior."

Verified directly against current code, not assumed: nomos-check-orchestration's Run (crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/run.rs) calls Check_Completeness_Mirrors and Check_Naming_Convention unconditionally over every source file every time -- there is no scope or rule selection anywhere in this workspace today, so CHK-001/CHK-002's selection mechanism does not exist yet, contrary to a first pass that assumed it did. What does exist and is genuinely unused: nomos-rules::RuleRegistry/RuleOffer (crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/registry.rs, OD-RULES-004), whose own module doc says plainly "Nothing here is consulted by Run(), and nothing here changes what runs on any given nomos check."

This increment is the smallest real slice: a new crate giving Gate its own seam (matching how WorkCommand/CheckCommand/SpecCommand each got one), implementing only Plan -- wiring a real RuleRegistry with both rules' real offers and reporting them, finally giving RuleRegistry a real consumer. Everything else WF-001 asks for (thresholds, waivers, approvals, blocking behavior, actual scope/rule filtering, run/explain/compare) is explicitly out of scope and left for later increments, the same shape P13-SPEC-ORCHESTRATION-1 used for SpecCommand's nine verbs.

One real wrinkle this increment must resolve, not paper over: Check_Naming_Convention has no CONTRACT_RECORD the way Check_Completeness_Mirrors cites D-134 -- naming.rs's own "# Why this has no CONTRACT_RECORD" section says its contract is README.md's Conventions section, prose rather than a versioned record. RuleOffer::contract_record/contract_record_version have no representation for that today. This item does not change RuleOffer's shape (OD-RULES-005 and OD-RULES-006 already declined extending it without a second real case, and this is not that case); it documents, at the one call site in the new crate that constructs naming's offer, what contract_record/contract_record_version hold for a record-less rule and why.
items.done_when: crates/orchestration/nomos-gate-orchestration exists at band 40 (sibling to nomos-work/check/spec-orchestration; depends only on nomos-rules and nomos-contracts, both well below 40, so it names none of its band-40 siblings and none of them may name it). GateCommand { root: PathBuf } (a struct, not an enum, matching CheckCommand's own precedent for "exactly one verb today"). A Registered() function builds a real RuleRegistry with two real RuleOffers: Check_Completeness_Mirrors's (rule nomos_rules::COMPLETENESS_MIRROR, contract_record nomos_rules::CONTRACT_RECORD, contract_record_version nomos_rules::CONTRACT_RECORD_VERSION -- read from the existing constants, not restated) and Check_Naming_Convention's (rule nomos_rules::NAMING_CONVENTION, contract_record "README.md", contract_record_version 0, with a doc comment at that construction site explaining 0 marks "no versioned record", citing naming.rs's own "why this has no CONTRACT_RECORD" section, and stating this is a local, revisitable choice rather than a claim about what RuleOffer's fields mean in general). GateOutcome::Planned(GatePlan) where GatePlan { rules: Vec<RuleOffer> } is Registered()'s two offers in RuleId order; GateOutcome::Contradictory(RuleRegistryError) if registration fails (structurally unreachable today with two distinct rule ids, kept for the same reason nomos-check-orchestration keeps CheckOutcome::Contradictory: a composition root's own defect must be representable, not unwound). A Run(&GateCommand) -> GateOutcome function. The crate's own module doc states plainly, the same way check-orchestration's and RuleRegistry's own docs do, that Plan does not yet filter by scope or rule (root is accepted and carried in GateCommand but not yet read), and that run/explain/compare do not exist yet as verbs -- this increment is Plan only. nomos-cli is not touched; nothing calls this crate yet, the same "additive and unwired" shape RuleRegistry itself has had since OD-RULES-004. Cargo.toml gains the workspace member; README.md's band table gains the row; tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs gains the band-40 declaration (naming none of its band-40 siblings as a dependency, and being named by none of them); tests/contract/surface gains the crate's blessed snapshot.

items.title: Whether heterogeneous rule populations justify a structured Rule Program/IR and global rule-compilation layer, or wait for two rules that actually need one
items.why: An external review of this workspace's dev branch argued nomos-proto (the retired Go predecessor) is 'almost a miniature proof' of a rule-compiler-plus-whole-program-optimizer architecture, and proposed registering that as a governing decision ahead of the Gate model. Verified directly against nomos-proto: no rule compiler, IR, or whole-program optimizer exists there -- it is independent Go judgment functions plus a shared driver/harness plus self-describing declarative metadata (Check, Rule, Inputs), and one of its own standards docs explicitly disclaims whole-program analysis. What the prototype does validate -- heterogeneous per-check dependencies (measured: 31/35/22/24 checks by input kind) and a shared driver extracted once real duplication existed (measured: sixteen checks) -- is evidence for explicit dependency declaration and demand-driven shared planning, which OD-RULES-005 and the analysis-planner roadmap item already cover, not evidence for a Rule IR. nomos-rules holds exactly two rules today (Check_Completeness_Mirrors, Check_Naming_Convention), neither exhibiting control flow, reusable subcomputations, or correction loops a capability requirement can't already express -- the same population-of-two shape OD-RULES-005/006 and OD-CAPABILITY-008 already declined to design ahead of. ARC-ROADMAP-001 stays as committed: Gate consumes canonical outcomes (findings/coverage/applicability) and is unaffected by whether a future rule's evidence comes from syntax, a dependency-graph capability, or eventually something requiring a richer program representation.
items.done_when: OD-RULES-007 is registered in crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/ with status: open (not accepted -- this logs the question and its triggers, it does not decide it), names the concrete triggers requiring two or more real rules to exhibit (shared multi-step derived computation not expressible as ordinary facts; rule-local control flow that must be planner-visible; correction/recheck loops with reusable semantics; reusable subworkflows/procedures; planner-visible native operations with declared effects; optimization opportunities fact-demand union alone can't obtain), explicitly corrects the record of what nomos-proto does and does not validate, and both diagram-set and domain-specification projections are re-rendered and pass their freshness checks (rendered/verified outside ledger territory, per OD-GATE-005).

items.title: Whether Gate's ScopeSelector and RuleSelector are built now, or wait for a caller that needs to select less than everything
items.why: ARC-ROADMAP-001 names ScopeSelector and RuleSelector as Gate's first two configurable policy types, and nomos-gate-orchestration's first increment (P13-GATE-ORCHESTRATION-1) deliberately left both unbuilt: GateCommand::root is accepted and carried, not read, and GatePlan reports every registered rule unconditionally. Verified directly against the real code: nomos-check-orchestration::Run (crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/run.rs) still calls both shipped rules unconditionally over every source it is handed, and only one language provider exists, so no real caller anywhere in this workspace demonstrates a need to select fewer than all rules or all files. OD-HOST-004 already decided the adjacent case -- Run stays hand-written until a rule's participation actually varies by request -- and building either selector now, on ARC-ROADMAP-001's naming alone, would repeat the exact machinery-before-demonstrated-need mistake D-135 already named, that OD-PACKAGE-006 and OD-PACKAGE-008 already declined for provider and rule registration. This is deliberately not covered by the user's 2026-08-18 override prioritizing plugin/package registration infrastructure: that override is about the registration seam, and RuleRegistry::Offer already lets any count of rules register unconditionally -- nothing about the selectors blocks independent plugin or package development, the same distinction that kept OD-RULES-005/006 and OD-CAPABILITY-007 as open questions rather than builds.

items.title: MemoryFactStore::Invalidate clones the whole dependents map every call; the hazard is real and left deferred rather than silently unaddressed
items.why: memory_store.rs:353 clones self.dependents (the reverse-dependency index over every fact this store has ever materialized a dependency edge for) on every single Invalidate call, regardless of how much of the graph that invalidation actually reaches. The comment right above it explains why -- DependencyPropagation::Spread takes an immutable &BTreeMap while its own on_reach callback needs &mut self for Invalidate_One and self.keys, a live conflict the borrow checker refuses without either cloning or restructuring the call -- but nothing records this as a measured, deliberately-accepted cost the way ARC-ROADMAP-001 already does in aggregate for six other confirmed nomos-analysis hazards. This session traced it to ground: it is real, it is O(the whole store's dependents map) per invalidation rather than O(what that invalidation reaches), and DependencyPropagation is a population-of-one seam (D-130/D-135/D-138) this workspace has already declined to redesign ahead of a second real implementation.
items.done_when: A new OD-ANALYSIS decision record states the hazard, why the clone exists (the borrow conflict), what was considered, and a concrete trigger for revisiting it (a second real DependencyPropagation implementation, or measured evidence the cost is live in a real run) -- registered as governing, related to ARC-ROADMAP-001, D-130, D-135 and D-138, with diagram-set and domain-specification re-rendered fresh from the publishing record set.

items.title: Gate's registry composes two of the three shipped rules, so nomos gate plan and nomos check disagree about what this workspace enforces
items.why:
Measured at 21838d4, not inferred. `nomos gate plan` prints `rules: 2`. `nomos-check-orchestration::run::Run` calls three -- Check_Completeness_Mirrors, Check_Naming_Convention and Check_Dependency_Direction, the last wired by P13-DEPENDENCY-WIRE-1. `nomos-gate-orchestration::composition::Registered` offers only the first two; DEPENDENCY_DIRECTION is exported from nomos_rules and never offered.

Gate's own lib.rs is honest about this and names it as separate work its increment did not do. Nothing else is. The board carries no item for it, and the board is otherwise empty -- so the one acknowledged gap in the newest crate is undiscoverable through the only place that is supposed to make work discoverable. That is the register the ledger exists to be.

It is also OD-GATE-001's shape. GatePlan is the answer to 'what rules exist' and it is now a smaller answer than the run it describes, which is worse than no answer: a caller reading the plan concludes dependency direction is unenforced when it is enforced on every check.

Four commits on 2026-08-19 swept the three-rule count through nomos-rules' lib.rs, dependency.rs, OD-RULES-007, OD-GATE-014, nomos-add-plugin and gate's lib.rs. The sweep corrected prose and left two claims standing: composition.rs's own function doc still says 'Registers this workspace's two shipped rules', and README.md's band table still says nomos-lang-rust-cargo is 'Not yet composed into nomos-check-orchestration::Run' when it is composed -- Cargo dependency, Provider_Offer, Materialize_Workspace and the rule call are all present. tests/contract asserts the band structure, not that sentence, which is why nothing caught it.

The citation is the part that is not merely mechanical. RuleOffer requires contract_record and contract_record_version. OD-PACKAGE-001 measured that an uncited rule left PKG-014's traceability requirement asserted in prose and nowhere in the crate, and tests/contract/tests/rule_contract_citation.rs is the mechanical check that closed it for D-134. Registering the third rule with an inline version literal nobody checks would reopen exactly that, one rule later. OD-RULES-003 is this rule's contract and it is a versioned record, so it can be cited properly, unlike Check_Naming_Convention's README.md sentinel.
items.done_when:
`nomos gate plan` reports three rules, and the plan's contents are asserted rather than counted.

Check_Dependency_Direction cites OD-RULES-003 by constants beside the rule, the shape mirror.rs already uses, not by a literal in the composition root. A version cited in a composition root drifts silently; a version cited beside the implementation is where whoever amends the record will be looking.

That citation is mechanically checked. rule_contract_citation.rs checks both shipped citations against the records' own front matter, not one of them, so the second is not a claim nothing verifies. Its own module doc says 'one shipped rule' and stops being true here.

composition.rs's function doc names three. The gate crate's own test stops being named Test_A_Plan_Should_Hold_Both_Shipped_Rules and asserts all three RuleOffers, in RuleId order, with the dependency rule's citation among them.

README.md's nomos-lang-rust-cargo row stops saying the provider is not composed.

The nomos-rules surface snapshot carries the new constants.

Not closed by registering the rule and leaving the citation unchecked, and not closed by editing the doc sentences without changing what Registered returns.

items.title: Three records' Status sections are the single word Accepted., which trips NSV-PRESERVE-004 and has had the gate's Test step red on dev since 2026-08-18
items.why:
Reproduced on a clean tree at 417fbcd, not inferred from a log:

  cargo test -p nomos-spec-validate --test preservation_holds
  Test_A_Seeded_Store_Should_Pass_Preservation_Non_Vacuously ... FAILED
  5 rule(s) ran over 5519 subject(s): 1 violation(s)
  [Violation { subject: '3 section(s) across 3 document(s)',
               detail: 'repeats an undeclared template: Accepted.' }]

The three are ARC-ROADMAP-001, OD-CONNECTOR-001 and OD-CONNECTOR-002. Each closes with a Status section whose entire body is the word 'Accepted.'

nomos_spec_ingest::SHARED_BY is 3. OD-CONNECTOR-001 and OD-CONNECTOR-002 have carried that body since 2026-08-16 (2eedd12, 947a834), which is two and under the threshold. ARC-ROADMAP-001 landed the third on 2026-08-18 in 62bb1ad. The gate's Test step has been red on dev since that commit.

It stayed invisible for a reason worth writing down rather than only fixing. nomos work finish runs the gate's Lint step plus the finishing item's own predicate -- not cargo test --workspace. Every item that landed after 62bb1ad had a predicate scoped to its own crates, none of which is nomos-spec-validate, so each one finished green over a workspace that was already red. The check that would have caught it is the one nobody runs between commits.

The rule is right and this is not a false positive to suppress. NSV-PRESERVE-004 exists because OD-SPEC-004 measured a v14-to-v15 migration hollowing 44 restored members with one undeclared adjective, and a one-word status body repeated verbatim across three unrelated governing records is exactly the form letter it names. Declaring 'Accepted.' in FILLER_PATTERNS would silence it by widening the definition of accounted-for filler, which is the opposite of what that list is for -- and FILLER_PATTERNS is itself already flagged by completeness-mirror as declaring no mirror.

The rest of this repository's records do not write Status this way. OD-GATE-009's says 'Closed. P11-PLATFORM-UNCHECKED carries it, and it discharges the fourth and last of the instances OD-GATE-006 measured.' The three above are the outliers, not the convention.
items.done_when:
cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-validate is green, and green because the three Status sections say something about the record they close rather than because the rule was widened to accept them.

Each of the three says what its own status is of -- what carries it, what it discharges, what would reopen it -- in the shape the other 137 records already use. Three sections that merely differ from each other while still saying nothing have moved the violation rather than answered it.

FILLER_PATTERNS is unchanged, and SHARED_BY is unchanged. Either edit would close the test by making the rule blind to the class it was written for.

The projection obligation is discharged, not deferred: three governing records move, so diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered per OD-GATE-005 from a detached worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes, and freshness reports both current there.

Separately, the hole that let this sit for a day is named. work finish's predicate scoping is why a red workspace kept finishing items green; whether that is a defect in finish, in how predicates are authored, or neither is a question this item may log as a record rather than answer -- but it is not left unwritten.

items.title: Seven guards fail whenever the board is at rest, so the gate's Test step is red on nearly every commit for a reason no commit contains
items.why:
Measured across the last 30 commits of dev, reading each commit's own committed work/ledger.json and counting open items whose territory reserves anything under docs/records:

  26 of 30 commits carry 0 or 1 open record writers
   3 of 30 carry 2 (ed03cf6, 1fa8a8c, ce76c96, all within seven minutes on 2026-08-18)

crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/records_do_not_serialize has seven assertions that fail below two. Reproduced on a clean tree at 4823e31: cargo test -p nomos-ledger --test records_do_not_serialize reports 7 passed, 7 failed, every failure of the form 'fewer than two open items reserve a record, so the concurrency this file measures cannot be observed; got 0'.

The gate's Test step is cargo test --workspace. CI checks out the commit, which carries the ledger as a file. So the step has been red on nearly every commit of this branch, and red for a reason that is not a property of the commit at all -- it is a property of which sessions happened to be mid-work when the commit was made. A gate answering a question about the committer's calendar is not a gate.

The guards are not wrong and this is not a request to delete them. OD-LEDGER-004 chose to read the real board deliberately: 'the defect was never in the comparison code, which had always compared paths correctly, so a fixture proving two invented territories disjoint would have passed on the day the board was fully blocked.' That reasoning is exactly right about the positive assertions. The anti-vacuity guards were then added on top, and nobody asked what they say about a board with nothing open -- which is not an edge case but the normal end state of finished work. The board is quiescent by design right now; every item on it is Done or Declined.

So two true things collide. A guard that lets an assertion pass over an empty subject is the defect this repository names most often -- 'a test that cannot find its corpus passes' is in AGENTS.md, and OD-GATE-001 is the record. And a guard whose verdict is a function of live coordination state makes a green tree impossible at rest, which is worse, because the failure is unrelated to anything the committer did and so trains everyone to ignore the step.

Precedent exists in this same gate for the shape that resolves it: the step named 'Corpus gates (reports what did not run)' reports an absence loudly instead of failing on it, and AGENTS.md points at tests/contract/ for the size of that hole. Absence reported is not absence hidden.
items.done_when:
cargo test --workspace is green on a tree whose board is quiescent, and still red on a board carrying the defect OD-LEDGER-004 closed.

Both halves are required and the second is the one that is easy to lose. Restoring docs/records to a single open item must still fail, and the item shows that measured -- not argued -- exactly as OD-LEDGER-004 showed it.

The record decides how an assertion over live coordination state is allowed to behave when that state is empty, and it decides it as a class rather than for these seven call sites. It says which of the three shapes each guard takes: an assertion that is honest over an empty board and stays an assertion; a non-vacuity proof moved to a reconstructed fixture, which OD-LEDGER-004 already builds for the pre-fix authoring; or an absence reported the way the gate's own corpus step reports one. It says what the losing shapes give up, not only what the winner buys.

Nothing is silenced. A guard that is deleted, downgraded to a warning nobody reads, or made conditional on an environment variable has hidden the class rather than answered it, and the record must say so about itself.

The 26-of-30 measurement is repeated after the change and stated: the point is that the number stops mattering, not that it improves.

OD-LEDGER-032 is written and registered under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/, and both required projections are re-rendered per OD-GATE-005 from a worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes.

Not closed by raising or lowering the threshold. Two is not the problem; reading a number that changes without the tree changing is.

items.title: Gate gains a first real run verb: walk, judge, and reduce to Passed/Failed/Indeterminate
items.why: ARC-ROADMAP-001 constraint 5, OD-GATE-014 and OD-GATE-015 all name the same trigger: Gate gaining a run verb that actually executes rules, rather than plan's report-only shape. 417fbcd (P13-GATE-REGISTRY-THIRD-RULE) closed the plan/check rule-count gap but explicitly did not touch run/explain/compare or any policy surface -- confirmed by re-reading its diff and nomos-gate-orchestration/src/lib.rs, which still says so. Both open decisions are otherwise blocked on this: neither ScopeSelector/RuleSelector nor BaselinePolicy/SuppressionPolicy has a caller whose behavior they would change until run exists to be filtered or to have its disposition altered.
items.done_when:
Disposition shape, settled before coding (per user direction) and verified against the real code rather than assumed:

GateRunOutcome { Passed, Failed, Indeterminate } lives in nomos-gate-orchestration (crates/orchestration/nomos-gate-orchestration/src/outcome.rs), alongside a pure function Disposition(findings: &[Finding]) -> GateRunOutcome that returns Failed if any finding.Can_Fail_A_Build(), Passed otherwise -- never Indeterminate, which only nomos-cli assigns, for CheckOutcome variants Disposition never sees.

Verified band constraint: nomos-gate-orchestration and nomos-check-orchestration are both band 40 (README.md), so gate-orchestration must not depend on check-orchestration (tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs's Test_Dependencies_Should_Run_Strictly_Downward requires dependency_band < band). GateRunResult { root, check_outcome: CheckOutcome, blocking_findings, disposition } therefore lives in nomos-cli (band 90, already depends on both peers), which walks the tree, calls nomos_check_orchestration::Run, and reduces:

  Judged { findings, .. }  -> disposition = nomos_gate_orchestration::Disposition(&findings); blocking_findings = findings filtered by Can_Fail_A_Build()
  Unreadable, Contradictory(_), NoSource, NoFacts { .. } -> disposition = Indeterminate, blocking_findings empty

Claim (coverage-debt/agent-required) rides in check_outcome for information only and does not affect disposition, matching OD-COMPLETENESS-004's existing choice that Claim is reported, not gated on.

Exit codes for the new  verb reuse the existing cross-group numbering nomos-cli's own exit_code.rs docs already state as binding (an exit code means one thing per binary): Ok=0 for Passed, Violations=1 for Failed (same meaning check::ExitCode::Violations already carries), Contradictory=5 extended to also cover CheckOutcome::Unreadable/Contradictory beneath a run (same meaning it already claims: the foundational thing could not be assembled), and a new Vacuous=6 for CheckOutcome::NoSource/NoFacts (same meaning check::ExitCode::Vacuous already carries). No new exit-code meaning is invented. Indeterminate is never exit 0, proving it does not collapse into Passed.

 is unchanged: Test_A_Real_Plan_Should_Report_All_Three_Shipped_Rules keeps passing without modification to its assertions. Test_An_Unimplemented_Verb_Should_Refuse (which currently asserts  is refused) is replaced --  is no longer unimplemented -- while  and  stay refused as usage, unchanged. parsing.rs's USAGE text and doc comment, gate.rs's own doc comment ('What this module does not do'), and nomos-gate-orchestration/src/lib.rs's doc comment are all corrected to stop saying  is unimplemented; they keep saying so for explain/compare/ScopeSelector/RuleSelector/CoveragePolicy/BaselinePolicy/SuppressionPolicy/phases/thresholds/waivers/approvals, none of which this item builds.

At least one real, non-synthetic test runs  (or the crate-internal equivalent) over this repository's own tree end to end and checks the disposition is structurally consistent with whether any rendered finding can fail a build, the same 'real run over the real tree' discipline Test_A_Real_Plan_Should_Report_All_Three_Shipped_Rules already uses for plan.

tests/contract/surface/nomos-gate-orchestration.txt is re-blessed for the new public items (GateRunOutcome, Disposition).

cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-cli is green, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings is clean.

Out of scope, named rather than silently skipped: explain, compare, ScopeSelector, RuleSelector, CoveragePolicy, BaselinePolicy, SuppressionPolicy, required phases, thresholds, waivers, approvals. This item's done_when does not require OD-GATE-014 or OD-GATE-015 to be resolved -- landing run is what gives them a real trigger to fire on, not a reason to fire them here.
