items.why: ARC-ROADMAP-001 constraint 5, OD-GATE-014 and OD-GATE-015 all name the same trigger: Gate gaining a `run` verb that actually executes rules, rather than `plan`'s report-only shape. `417fbcd` (P13-GATE-REGISTRY-THIRD-RULE) closed the plan/check rule-count gap but explicitly did not touch run/explain/compare or any policy surface -- confirmed by re-reading its diff and `nomos-gate-orchestration/src/lib.rs`, which still says so. Both open decisions are otherwise blocked on this: neither ScopeSelector/RuleSelector nor BaselinePolicy/SuppressionPolicy has a caller whose behavior they would change until `run` exists to be filtered or to have its disposition altered.
items.done_when:
Disposition shape, settled before coding (per user direction) and verified against the real code rather than assumed:

`GateRunOutcome { Passed, Failed, Indeterminate }` lives in nomos-gate-orchestration (crates/orchestration/nomos-gate-orchestration/src/outcome.rs), alongside a pure function `Disposition(findings: &[Finding]) -> GateRunOutcome` that returns `Failed` if any `finding.Can_Fail_A_Build()`, `Passed` otherwise -- never `Indeterminate`, which only nomos-cli assigns, for `CheckOutcome` variants `Disposition` never sees.

Verified band constraint: nomos-gate-orchestration and nomos-check-orchestration are both band 40 (README.md), so gate-orchestration must not depend on check-orchestration (tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs's Test_Dependencies_Should_Run_Strictly_Downward requires dependency_band < band). `GateRunResult { root, check_outcome: CheckOutcome, blocking_findings, disposition }` therefore lives in nomos-cli (band 90, already depends on both peers), which walks the tree, calls `nomos_check_orchestration::Run`, and reduces:

  Judged { findings, .. }  -> disposition = nomos_gate_orchestration::Disposition(&findings); blocking_findings = findings filtered by Can_Fail_A_Build()
  Unreadable, Contradictory(_), NoSource, NoFacts { .. } -> disposition = Indeterminate, blocking_findings empty

Claim (coverage-debt/agent-required) rides in check_outcome for information only and does not affect disposition, matching OD-COMPLETENESS-004's existing choice that Claim is reported, not gated on.

Exit codes for the new `run` verb reuse the existing cross-group numbering nomos-cli's own exit_code.rs docs already state as binding (an exit code means one thing per binary): Ok=0 for Passed, Violations=1 for Failed (same meaning check::ExitCode::Violations already carries), Contradictory=5 extended to also cover CheckOutcome::Unreadable/Contradictory beneath a run (same meaning it already claims: the foundational thing could not be assembled), and a new Vacuous=6 for CheckOutcome::NoSource/NoFacts (same meaning check::ExitCode::Vacuous already carries). No new exit-code meaning is invented. Indeterminate is never exit 0, proving it does not collapse into Passed.

`plan` is unchanged: Test_A_Real_Plan_Should_Report_All_Three_Shipped_Rules keeps passing without modification to its assertions. Test_An_Unimplemented_Verb_Should_Refuse (which currently asserts `run` is refused) is replaced -- `run` is no longer unimplemented -- while `explain` and `compare` stay refused as usage, unchanged. parsing.rs's USAGE text and doc comment, gate.rs's own doc comment ("What this module does not do"), and nomos-gate-orchestration/src/lib.rs's doc comment are all corrected to stop saying `run` is unimplemented; they keep saying so for explain/compare/ScopeSelector/RuleSelector/CoveragePolicy/BaselinePolicy/SuppressionPolicy/phases/thresholds/waivers/approvals, none of which this item builds.

At least one real, non-synthetic test runs `nomos gate run --root .` (or the crate-internal equivalent) over this repository's own tree end to end and checks the disposition is structurally consistent with whether any rendered finding can fail a build, the same "real run over the real tree" discipline Test_A_Real_Plan_Should_Report_All_Three_Shipped_Rules already uses for plan.

cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-cli is green, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings is clean.

Out of scope, named rather than silently skipped: explain, compare, ScopeSelector, RuleSelector, CoveragePolicy, BaselinePolicy, SuppressionPolicy, required phases, thresholds, waivers, approvals. items.why:
`OD-GATE-014` and `OD-GATE-015` each name "`Gate` gaining a `run` verb" as an independent trigger for revisiting whether `ScopeSelector`/`RuleSelector` and `BaselinePolicy`/`SuppressionPolicy` are built now. `P13-GATE-RUN-FIRST-INCREMENT-3` landed that verb. Both records' prose still describes `run` as hypothetical ("Gate's only implemented verb (Plan) is report-only"), which is now false, and their own stated trigger fired -- they need to be read again with the real thing in front of them, not left stale.

Read again rather than assumed: `run`'s real shape (walk unconditionally, judge everything, reduce through `Can_Fail_A_Build`) resolves the *design* risk both records named -- shaping a selector or a policy type around a `run` that might not match what got built. It does not resolve the *deeper* condition each record was really waiting on: a real caller whose build `run`'s output actually affects. Verified directly against `.github/workflows/gate.yml`, not assumed: the `Rules` step (`OD-GATE-004`'s own CI step) still invokes `cargo run --quiet -p nomos-cli --bin nomos -- check --root .` -- `nomos check` directly, not `nomos gate run` or `nomos gate plan`. `Gate` has a real `run` verb with nobody calling it. That is not the same claim as "the trigger has not fired" -- it has, in the narrow sense both records named it -- but it is not the same claim as "build the selectors or the policy types now" either, which neither record's own logic supports without a caller whose behavior they would change.

items.title: OD-GATE-014 and OD-GATE-015: gate run's Rules-step caller landed, and it fires one record's trigger but not the other's
items.why:
P13-GATE-RUN-CI-CALLER (24e6cea) switched .github/workflows/gate.yml's Rules step from invoking `nomos check` directly to invoking `nomos gate run`, giving Gate's run verb its first real caller. Both OD-GATE-014 and OD-GATE-015 were left describing that step as still invoking `nomos check` directly -- true when each was last revised, false now, verified against the real workflow file rather than assumed. This is the same kind of staleness P13-GATE-014-015-RUN-TRIGGER-FIRED itself corrected one landing ago, for the same two records, and the same discipline applies: read them again against the real thing rather than leave them describing a caller that no longer exists.

The two records are not affected equally. OD-GATE-015's own named trigger -- "a real caller whose build run's disposition gates" -- is exactly what this caller is: Actions fails the Rules step (and so the whole gate job) on any non-zero exit, and gate run's exit code now comes from Disposition's reduction rather than from check's exit code taken directly. That is this record's first trigger fired, in the full sense, not the narrower "run exists" sense P13-GATE-014-015-RUN-TRIGGER-FIRED recorded. OD-GATE-014's own trigger is a caller that needs to evaluate fewer than every rule or fewer than every file -- CI still runs `gate run --root .` unconditionally over everything, the identical shape it always judged, so switching which subcommand runs it does not fire OD-GATE-014's trigger at all. items.why:
P13-GATE-RUN-CI-CALLER (24e6cea) switched .github/workflows/gate.yml's Rules step from invoking `nomos check --root .` directly to invoking `nomos gate run --root .`. Two doc comments in crates/host/nomos-cli, verified directly against the real files rather than assumed, still describe the old wiring as current.

check.rs's own module doc, under "# This command is a gate step now, and that changes what an exit code costs", states "OD-GATE-004 wired the Rules step of .github/workflows/gate.yml to cargo run --quiet -p nomos-cli --bin nomos -- check --root ." and then narrates check::ExitCode's variants as literally "what each code now does to a pull request" -- both false since P13-GATE-RUN-CI-CALLER. The design reasoning (zero is the only success, a sixth code must survive, Vacuous must never be renumbered) is still true of check::ExitCode itself and still worth keeping, but the claim that this module's exit code is what CI observes directly is not: CI now observes gate::ExitCode (crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/exit_code.rs), which deliberately carries the identical meanings forward one hop away, through CheckOutcome consumed inside gate/run.rs.

gate/tests.rs's Test_A_Real_Run_Should_Judge_This_Workspaces_Own_Tree carries a doc comment and an assert failure message both claiming "this repository's own gate step already runs/requires nomos check --root . to exit clean" as the reason `run` must agree with it. This is the same shape as the many already-closed P13-*-STALE corrections in this ledger (e.g. P13-CLI-CARGO-GATE-COMMENT-STALE, P13-LANG-RUST-CARGO-DOC-STALE): a doc comment describing a caller's reach that drifted true after a related landing.

items.title: OD-CAPABILITY-008: a third provider joins, and Materialize diverges from PROVIDER/Declared_Guarantee/FactContext for a principled reason
items.why:
OD-CAPABILITY-008 (authored 2026-08-18, status open) named its own trigger plainly: "revisit when a third provider joins." crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-cargo was built and composed into nomos-check-orchestration's Registered() (P13-DEPENDENCY-EDGES-2, P13-DEPENDENCY-WIRE-1) after the record was written -- verified directly against the real code, not assumed: it is a third live implementation of the PROVIDER/Declared_Guarantee/Materialize/FactContext convention the record analyzes. The trigger has fired and nothing has read the record against it yet -- grepped the full ledger, nothing references OD-CAPABILITY-008 since it was authored.

What the third instance actually shows, checked field by field rather than assumed: PROVIDER (&str), Declared_Guarantee() -> Guarantee (identical pub const fn signature verified across all three guarantee.rs files) and FactContext (identical four fields -- snapshot, variant, configuration, generation, same types -- verified across all three provider.rs files) agree exactly across all three providers. Materialize does not: nomos_lang_rust_cargo::Materialize_Workspace(root: &Path, context: FactContext) -> Result<Vec<PackageFact>, MetadataError> takes no SubjectId (it discovers every workspace member's subject itself) and returns many facts per call, where the first two providers' Materialize takes a subject: SubjectId, source: &str and returns one fact per call (with return type already varying between those two by fallibility -- Materialization enum vs MaterializedFact directly). This is exactly the shape of divergence the record's own "Current Position" section speculated a third provider might reveal ("a Materialize taking its context by a different shape than the other two share"), and it is principled rather than accidental: nomos-lang-rust-cargo is a whole-workspace capability, the first two are per-file capabilities, and Materialize's shape tracks that real difference in what each capability is of.

"What Would Decide It" is rewritten to say the trigger fired and narrows the question rather than resolving it: a trait over exactly PROVIDER/Declared_Guarantee/FactContext now has three checked instances to be built against; a trait attempting to also cover Materialize would have to invent a shape general enough to admit both "one fact from one named subject" and "many facts from one discovered root", which the record explicitly declines to endorse building speculatively, citing the same reasoning it already gave for keeping Encode_Payload undeduplicated.

items.title: nomos-lang-rust's corpus test cannot explain a misplaced inner doc comment, and a stray agent worktree doubles its refusal count
items.why:
cargo test -p nomos-lang-rust --test corpus, run against the real corpus (NOMOS_RUST_CORPUS=F:/repos/xvpe, or its DEFAULT_ROOT fallback which happens to resolve on this machine), fails Test_Every_Refusal_Should_Be_Named_And_Explained. Reproduced directly: 4 of 17369 files refused, 0 explained by the one known reason (a stray byte order mark) this test's own doc comment names, all 4 UNEXPLAINED.

Two distinct, independent causes, both verified directly rather than assumed:

1. crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/tests/corpus/walk.rs's NOT_SOURCE list excludes `target` and `.git` but not `.claude`. This xvpe checkout carries a stray agent worktree under .claude/worktrees/agent-a4b4daaf1328e4f69/, itself a checked-out copy of (part of) the same tree, so the same two real files are walked twice -- once at their real path, once again under the worktree -- doubling every count that touches them, including this test's refusal count (2 real refusals reported as 4).

2. The two real files (crates/engine/foundations/xvpe-thread-pool/benches/fiber/throughput_context_stack_pool.rs and .../throughput_wait_scaling_wakeup.rs) each place a `//!` inner doc comment after `use super::*;`. Read directly: this is invalid under Rust's own grammar, not a gap in this provider's parser -- inner attributes and inner doc comments must precede every other item in their scope, in any position, so rustc would refuse these two files as well. This is the corpus growing a new kind of damage, in the sense this test's own doc comment already names as one of the two possible causes ("Either the corpus grew a new kind of damage or this provider has fallen behind the language, and the two need different responses") -- and the response for damage, not a provider gap, is to name and explain it the same way a stray byte order mark already is, not to change what this provider accepts.

This test is corpus-gated and CI never runs it (no NOMOS_RUST_CORPUS is set in .github/workflows/gate.yml), so this failure is invisible there and only reproduces on a machine holding a real xvpe checkout -- this is such a machine. The test's own purpose, stated in its doc comment, is exactly to catch this: "a refusal this walk cannot attribute to a stray mark is a new fact and fails the test." It did its job.
items.done_when:
walk.rs's NOT_SOURCE gains ".claude", with its doc comment explaining why: a worktree checked out under .claude/worktrees/ duplicates real source under a hidden directory nobody authored, the same "not somebody's source" reasoning target and .git already state. Every file this repository's own walk touches under that directory is scratch state, not a second copy of the corpus.

claims.rs's Unexplained (or a sibling helper) gains a second recognized refusal category alongside the existing stray-byte-order-mark check: a `//!` or `#![...]` inner doc comment/attribute appearing after a real item already began the file. The check is textual (line-scan for the first `//!`/`#![` line that follows an earlier non-comment, non-blank line), mirroring the existing byte-order-mark check's own level of precision, not a second parse. The eprintln! per-refusal report names which of the two reasons applied ("stray byte order mark" / "misplaced inner doc comment" / "UNEXPLAINED"), and the doc comment on Test_Every_Refusal_Should_Be_Named_And_Explained ("What this corpus actually refuses") is rewritten with fresh, actually-measured counts and both reasons -- not left describing only the historical byte-order-mark case, since re-measuring after the .claude exclusion shows that reason no longer occurring in this corpus at all.

Territory is exactly crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/tests/corpus/walk.rs and crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/tests/corpus/claims.rs. No change to any file under crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/src -- this provider's own parsing is correct; only the corpus test's own accounting changes.

items.title: Whether docs/records needs a distinct result-record type, or the doubling in OD-LEDGER-017 is unmeasured rather than costly
items.why: An external design review (nomos_spec_and_work_ledger_arch.txt, reviewed this session) proposes splitting a completed unit of work into four artifact kinds -- task, change record, ADR, and result record -- so a durable decision (why), a semantic delta (what changed and why the intent moved), and a delivery report (what was actually built, against which commit) never share one file. docs/records/ has one type today: a governing record (architecture/decision/correction/validation/cleanup, matching LedgerItem::kind) that carries decision content and delivery narrative in the same file when the two coincide. OD-LEDGER-017 is the concrete instance: it states a decision (all six WORK-LEDGER requirements bind), narrates what was measured (216 v14 task files, the review that produced the six requirements), and reports verdicts per requirement, in one record with one status. Whether that doubling is a real cost or a distinction without a difference is unmeasured: no record in docs/records/ has visibly needed independent revision of its narrative content versus its decision content, and no ledger item has been blocked by lacking a separate place for 'what was actually delivered.'

items.title: Whether actual impact should be recorded against declared territory, or territory being declared not enforced makes the drift unmeasured rather than owed
items.why: An external design review (nomos_spec_and_work_ledger_arch.txt, reviewed this session) recommends recording actual touched paths/symbols against a task's expected impact at completion, flagging expansion beyond declared scope, on the argument that it improves future planning and catches undeclared scope creep before it collides with another claim. LedgerItem's Territory declares expected paths and patterns, and OD-LEDGER-001 already states territory is declared, not enforced -- nothing stops a write into a claimed path, so a finished item's actual diff can silently exceed its declared Territory today and nothing records that it did. Whether this is a real, currently-occurring gap or a theoretical one is unmeasured: no incident of an item's actual impact exceeding its declared territory has been checked against git history for this board.

items.title: Which semantic domain the next production rule needs, and which deferred architecture piece it actually forces
items.why: The board is quiescent -- work list reports next: nothing is eligible, and every P13 item is Done or Declined. The three shipped rules (Check_Naming_Convention, Check_Completeness_Mirrors, Check_Dependency_Direction) span only syntax-local judgment, cross-artifact consistency, and package-dependency graph reachability -- none touches resolved types, control flow, dataflow, or architecture-boundary facts. OD-RULES-005, OD-RULES-006, OD-RULES-007, OD-GATE-014, OD-CAPABILITY-008 and OD-PACKAGE-006/008 all declined to build a deferred abstraction (a measured Inputs classification, EnforcementPlacementRationale, a Rule Program/IR, ScopeSelector/RuleSelector, a provider trait, generic registration bases) ahead of a real case demonstrating the need, and each named the concrete trigger that would revisit it. This item follows the same discipline in the other direction: rather than re-litigating an already-declined abstraction, it picks one concrete next rule from an unrepresented semantic domain and lets that rule's actual requirements be the evidence for whether any deferred piece is now forced -- decided from the requirement, not in advance of it.

Status is left open if nothing is forced, or names the concrete next capability item if something is, following OD-CAPABILITY-008's precedent of narrowing rather than resolving. Closed by the record alone: no crate changes. diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md (with sidecars) are re-rendered and pass nomos spec freshness --require diagram-set --require domain-specification, verified from an isolated worktree holding exactly the record set this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005.

items.title: nomos-lang-rust-cargo shells out to cargo metadata with raw std::process::Command instead of nomos-platform's ProcessLauncher port
items.why: crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-cargo/src/metadata.rs::Run_Cargo_Metadata calls std::process::Command::new(cargo).output() directly. nomos-platform (band 15, already below this crate's band 25) declares exactly a ProcessLauncher port for this -- an argv Command with timeout/idle-timeout and a working_directory, returning captured stdout/stderr and a typed ExitOutcome that distinguishes a real exit from TimedOut/Stalled/Terminated rather than collapsing them. StdProcessLauncher already implements it without the pipe-buffer deadlock an earlier ledger item recorded (Drain_Into spawns a reader thread per stream), and nomos-work-orchestration::Run already establishes the exact idiom this fix follows: a generic P: ProcessLauncher parameter threaded from the composition root, so the orchestration crate depends only on nomos-platform and not nomos-platform-std. nomos-cli already owns a StdProcessLauncher instance (work.rs) and is the only caller of nomos_check_orchestration::Run (check.rs:137, gate/run.rs:60), so both call sites can pass it with no new composition-root state. The crate's own lib.rs doc names this as the one provider in the check composition with I/O of its own, but justifies that only against sources already read, never against the port this workspace already built for exactly this. Verified in session: no record or open ledger item addresses this bypass specifically.
items.done_when: Discover_Workspace and Materialize_Workspace (nomos-lang-rust-cargo) and Materialize_Dependencies and Run (nomos-check-orchestration) each gain a generic P: nomos_platform::ProcessLauncher parameter, following nomos_work_orchestration::Run's own pattern; Run_Cargo_Metadata builds a nomos_platform::Command (argv, working_directory = Some(root), a named timeout constant) and calls launcher.Run(&command) instead of std::process::Command, mapping a non-success ExitOutcome (TimedOut/Stalled/Terminated/non-zero Exited) to MetadataError with a reason distinguishing which; nomos-cli's check.rs and gate/run.rs pass &StdProcessLauncher at both call sites, matching work.rs's existing usage; nomos-lang-rust-cargo's own unit tests in metadata.rs and provider.rs pass a real StdProcessLauncher (nomos-platform-std added as a dev-dependency) and keep exercising this repository's own real workspace; lib.rs, provider.rs and nomos-check-orchestration's facts.rs/run.rs doc comments are updated to describe the process launch as going through the injected port rather than raw std::process::Command, preserving the existing I/O-vs-pure-bytes distinction; tests/contract/surface/nomos-lang-rust-cargo.txt and tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt are reblessed for the new signatures; cargo test -p nomos-lang-rust-cargo -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-cli -p nomos-contract-tests and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings both pass.

items.title: A single refactor commit clobbered six real lint-allow attributes with a stray // PROBE line, in six files plus three more with no clobbered attribute
items.why: git log -S'// PROBE' traces the marker to commit 8e1a793 ('refactor', 89 files, mostly blank-line noise) plus one file (nomos-corrections/src/lib.rs) where it was present since that crate's own first commit 206be26. Nothing in the repository greps, asserts on, or documents '// PROBE' as a convention -- verified by searching tests/, .github/, and every doc. In six files, 8e1a793 did not add noise beside a real line, it replaced one: crates/kernel/nomos-store/src/lib.rs and crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/src/lib.rs each lost #![allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)], crates/substrate/nomos-workspace/src/lib.rs lost the same, and crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/exclusion_holds/board.rs plus crates/substrate/nomos-workspace/tests/portable/{walk,permutation,arrival}.rs each lost #![allow(dead_code)]. Verified in session, not assumed: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes clean at current HEAD with none of those six attributes present, so nothing here is silently red today -- whatever made each allow necessary at the time it was added no longer applies, and this item is a pure text removal, not a revert. nomos-corrections/src/lib.rs and nomos-substrate's two remaining sites (crates/substrate/nomos-workspace/src/lib.rs already counted) round out the nine total files T-PROBE-FREE's own reason field already distinguishes from this -- that item was a stray board-write probe against work/ledger.json, an unrelated use of the same English word, not this code convention.

items.title: Build nomos.cap.controlflow.reachability's tier-1 heuristic provider and Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding, per OD-RULES-008
items.why: OD-RULES-008's own Status names the concrete next step: 'The concrete next capability item, should one be claimed, is that provider -- nomos.cap.controlflow.reachability or equivalent, scoped to intraprocedural reachability from a fact-read failure to a Finding-construction site -- with Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding as its first and, at first, only consumer.' Checked directly against nomos-capability's own resolution code (crates/substrate/nomos-capability/src/registry.rs Selected, src/resolution/selection.rs): a floor decides which offers are usable before Selection ever ranks among them, so a rule whose Requirement asks above every installed offer's guarantee gets Unmet::BelowRequirement, not a fallback -- Require_Any walks Selection::Weaker() among offers that already cleared the floor, not offers beneath it. So OD-RULES-008's own tier-1/tier-2 framing has to be read as an authorial choice at the rule, not a mechanical SupportedWithFallback: this item's Requirement asks for exactly FactVariant::Syntactic, what a heuristic AST-pattern-match tier actually delivers, and reports each finding as Applicability::PartiallySupported -- evaluated over part of the subject (the syntactically obvious wrong shapes), not the whole question OD-RULES-008's sound tier states. nomos-add-plugin's own skill (section 2) requires a capability contract that names a shape no existing capability carries to get its own crate below every provider, the same position nomos-cap-syntax and nomos-cap-dependency hold; this is a new capability (no statement, expression, branch or call-site record exists in nomos.cap.syntax.items' schema, confirmed against crates/capabilities/nomos-cap-syntax/src/payload.rs), so it gets one.
items.done_when: crates/capabilities/nomos-cap-controlflow declares capability nomos.cap.controlflow.reachability (schema nomos.controlflow.reachability.v1), matching nomos-cap-dependency's shape (Capability(), CONTRACT_VERSION, Payload_Schema(), Ceiling(), Capability_Contract()), with Ceiling() honestly stated at FactVariant::Syntactic, soundness Assurance::Sound (every shape this tier flags is a real, provable defect with no name or type resolution needed to see it), completeness Assurance::Unsound (known, by this item's own design, to miss every shape it does not pattern-match), IncrementalGranularity::File; and Encode_Payload/Parse_Payload round-trip a ReachabilityPayload{ sites: Vec<ReachabilitySite{ function, binding, shape }> } where shape is one of exactly Empty, BareContinue, BareReturn, TailOk. nomos-lang-rust gains a second capability offer (same PROVIDER constant, a new Declared_Guarantee/Provider_Offer pair naming this capability) whose Materialize walks one file's syn::ExprMatch arms via a new syn::visit::Visit walker (crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/src/reachability.rs and reachability/walk.rs, not extending the existing item-level Walk) for the pattern Err(applicability) => <body> -- exactly the binding name found three times in crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/{naming.rs:78,mirror/index.rs:74,dependency.rs:168} -- and records a ReachabilitySite naming the nearest enclosing function for every such arm whose body is syntactically empty, a bare continue, a bare return with no value, or a tail Ok(...) call, and records nothing for any other shape. crates/rules/nomos-rules gains Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding(sources: &[SourceFile], facts: &mut dyn FactReader) -> Vec<Finding>, signature-matching the other three rules, whose own Requirement asks for exactly FactVariant::Syntactic (not an aspirational floor nothing installed can clear -- see this item's why), whose Payload_Of reports a real Unread finding on a failed Require the same shape dependency.rs:168 does, and whose Violations_In emits one Finding per recorded ReachabilitySite with Applicability::PartiallySupported and a summary naming the function, the shape found, and why it is the exact defect Applicability's own module doc calls 'unknown is not pass'; cites OD-RULES-008 (this item's amendment, at the version it lands at) as its contract record, the same _CONTRACT_RECORD/_CONTRACT_RECORD_VERSION shape dependency.rs uses, checked live by tests/contract/tests/rule_contract_citation.rs. OD-RULES-008 is amended: its Status section states plainly that the tier-1 provider and rule now exist, names their real identifiers (nomos.cap.controlflow.reachability, Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding), and states that tier 2 (FactVariant::SemanticallyResolved, sound) remains unbuilt -- the part of its own original claim this item does not close. Neither the new rule nor the new provider is wired into nomos-gate-orchestration::Registered() or nomos-check-orchestration::Run -- reserving either file is out of this item's territory, and wiring is a follow-on the same way P13-DEPENDENCY-WIRE-1 followed P13-DEPENDENCY-EDGES-2. The new crate is declared at band 23 in Cargo.toml, README.md and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs (alongside nomos-cap-syntax and nomos-cap-dependency); tests/contract/surface gains a blessed snapshot for nomos-cap-controlflow and re-blessed snapshots for nomos-lang-rust and nomos-rules; tests/integration/tests/determinism/{declarations,domains}.rs register the new fact production (reusing SyntaxFactProduction::STRENGTH if its determinism claim genuinely matches, stating why in a doc comment if it does not). diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md (with sidecars) are re-rendered and pass nomos spec freshness --require diagram-set --require domain-specification, verified from an isolated worktree holding exactly the record set this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005.

items.title: nomos-lang-rust-cargo shells out to cargo metadata with raw std::process::Command instead of nomos-platform's ProcessLauncher port
items.why:
crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-cargo/src/metadata.rs::Run_Cargo_Metadata calls std::process::Command::new(cargo).output() directly. nomos-platform (band 15, already below this crate's band 25) declares exactly a ProcessLauncher port for this -- an argv Command with timeout/idle-timeout and a working_directory, returning captured stdout/stderr and a typed ExitOutcome that distinguishes a real exit from TimedOut/Stalled/Terminated rather than collapsing them. StdProcessLauncher already implements it without the pipe-buffer deadlock an earlier ledger item recorded (Drain_Into spawns a reader thread per stream), and nomos-work-orchestration::Run already establishes the exact idiom this fix follows: a generic P: ProcessLauncher parameter threaded from the composition root, so the orchestration crate depends only on nomos-platform and not nomos-platform-std. nomos-cli already owns a StdProcessLauncher instance (work.rs) and is the only caller of nomos_check_orchestration::Run (check.rs:137, gate/run.rs:60), so both call sites can pass it with no new composition-root state. The crate's own lib.rs doc names this as the one provider in the check composition with I/O of its own, but justifies that only against sources already read, never against the port this workspace already built for exactly this. Verified in session: no record or open ledger item addresses this bypass specifically.

Successor of P13-CARGO-METADATA-PROCESSLAUNCHER, abandoned for exactly this: Materialize_Workspace's signature also reaches crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-cargo/tests/invalidation.rs and tests/integration/tests/determinism/productions.rs, plus tests/integration/Cargo.toml for the launcher dev-dependency, none of which the first territory reserved.
items.done_when: Discover_Workspace and Materialize_Workspace (nomos-lang-rust-cargo) and Materialize_Dependencies and Run (nomos-check-orchestration) each gain a generic P: nomos_platform::ProcessLauncher parameter, following nomos_work_orchestration::Run's own pattern; Run_Cargo_Metadata builds a nomos_platform::Command (argv, working_directory = Some(root), a named timeout constant) and calls launcher.Run(&command) instead of std::process::Command, mapping a non-success ExitOutcome (TimedOut/Stalled/Terminated/non-zero Exited) to MetadataError with a reason distinguishing which; nomos-cli's check.rs and gate/run.rs pass &StdProcessLauncher at both call sites, matching work.rs's existing usage; every existing caller of Discover_Workspace/Materialize_Workspace -- nomos-lang-rust-cargo's own unit tests in metadata.rs and provider.rs, crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-cargo/tests/invalidation.rs, and tests/integration/tests/determinism/productions.rs -- passes a real StdProcessLauncher (nomos-platform-std added as a dev-dependency wherever it is not already present) and keeps exercising this repository's own real workspace; lib.rs, provider.rs and nomos-check-orchestration's facts.rs/run.rs doc comments are updated to describe the process launch as going through the injected port rather than raw std::process::Command, preserving the existing I/O-vs-pure-bytes distinction; tests/contract/surface/nomos-lang-rust-cargo.txt and tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt are reblessed for the new signatures; cargo test -p nomos-lang-rust-cargo -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-cli -p nomos-contract-tests -p nomos-integration-tests and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings both pass.

items.title: OD-PACKAGE-008: its named trigger fires twice (dependency and reachability contract citations), reassess against the four-rule population
items.why:
OD-PACKAGE-008 (status accepted, version 3) named its own revisit trigger plainly in its Status section: "Revisit again if a third rule, or Check_Naming_Convention itself, is found to need a version-bearing contract citation." Checked directly against the real code, not assumed: two more rules have landed under crates/rules/nomos-rules/src since version 3 was written. Check_Dependency_Direction (dependency.rs:149) cites DEPENDENCY_CONTRACT_RECORD = "OD-RULES-003" / DEPENDENCY_CONTRACT_RECORD_VERSION = 1 (dependency.rs:62,65). Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding (reachability.rs:92) cites UNREAD_REACHES_FINDING_CONTRACT_RECORD = "OD-RULES-008" / UNREAD_REACHES_FINDING_CONTRACT_RECORD_VERSION = 2 (reachability.rs:53,57). Both are version-bearing contract citations, mechanically checked by tests/contract/tests/rule_contract_citation.rs the same way the record's own text says D-134's citation is. The named trigger has fired twice over and nothing has read the record against it since -- grepped work/ledger.json for OD-PACKAGE-008, no item references it after P13-PACKAGE-008-... landed version 3.

The record's own Resolution and Status sections still discuss only the original two-rule (Check_Completeness_Mirrors / Check_Naming_Convention) comparison and do not mention dependency.rs or reachability.rs at all. Re-reading the population at four rules rather than two, checked field by field against ARCH-002's contents list, shows the version-3 comparison's own convergent/divergent split no longer describes the real population: "required canonical capabilities," which version 3 found unchanged between the first two rules (both nomos_cap_syntax via crate::Syntax_Requirement()), is no longer convergent across four -- Check_Dependency_Direction requires nomos_cap_dependency (Dependency_Requirement: FactVariant::SemanticallyResolved, Sound/Sound, IncrementalGranularity::Project) and Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding requires nomos_cap_controlflow (Reachability_Requirement: FactVariant::Syntactic, Sound/Unknown, IncrementalGranularity::File) -- two more distinct capability families, not variations on one shape. A field version 3 never had to examine because it had not yet diverged -- applicability semantics -- has now diverged structurally: Check_Completeness_Mirrors, Check_Naming_Convention and Check_Dependency_Direction all raise Applicability::Supported for a genuine violation (dependency.rs:281); Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding structurally never does -- every violation it raises carries Applicability::PartiallySupported (reachability.rs:185), by the rule's own stated design, because its tier-1 heuristic provider answers only part of its own question. Meanwhile the field the trigger actually named -- identity/version and normative specification, the contract-citation pair -- has moved from a 1-of-2 split version 3 read as unsettled to a 3-of-4 split (mirror/dependency/reachability cite a versioned record; naming remains the sole, deliberately documented exception, per its own module doc's "Why this has no CONTRACT_RECORD" section) -- materially more evidence the field itself is stable, which argues the opposite direction from the other two fields' new divergence.
items.done_when:
OD-PACKAGE-008 is edited through nomos spec preview / nomos spec commit (never hand-edited), front matter version bumps 3 -> 4, and it stays status: accepted -- this item settles what the four-rule population now shows, the same discipline P13-CAPABILITY-008-THIRD-PROVIDER-LANDED and P13-GATE-014-015-RUN-CALLER-LANDED already applied to sibling records, not a decision made in advance of reading the evidence.

The record gains a new section, after "Resolution" and before "Status," naming the fired trigger and redoing the field-by-field comparison at a population of four rather than reaffirming the population-of-two outcome by citation count alone: states plainly that the named trigger fired twice (Check_Dependency_Direction's OD-RULES-003/v1 and Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding's OD-RULES-008/v2 citations, both real and mechanically checked); states that identity/version and normative specification -- the field the trigger names -- moved from a 1-of-2 split to 3-of-4 (naming remains the sole, documented exception), which is more evidence for that field's stability, not less; states that required canonical capabilities, which the version-3 text found unchanged between the first two rules, is no longer convergent across four -- dependency and reachability each require a distinct capability family (nomos_cap_dependency, nomos_cap_controlflow) with distinct FactVariant/Assurance/IncrementalGranularity shapes, named specifically; states that applicability semantics, a field version 3 did not need to examine, has newly diverged -- three rules raise Applicability::Supported for a genuine violation, Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding structurally never does, always PartiallySupported, by its own stated tier-1 design; and states what still converges across all four with no exception -- the Payload_Of/Violations_In judgment split each later rule's own doc comment cites as reused from the one before it, EvidenceClass::Derived, and the complete absence across all four of any real instance of an optional enhanced implementation, an external diagnostic mapping, a correction/suppression contract, an evaluation corpus or agent-guidance fragments.

Resolution does not reverse: no nomos-rule-package crate is scaffolded now. The new section says why the reasoning is corrected rather than merely reaffirmed -- one of the two axes the original wait rested on (contract-citation instability) is no longer well supported by the real population, but two others (capability-requirement shape, applicability semantics) newly diverged as the population grew from two rules to four, and roughly half of ARCH-002's contents list has zero real instance across every rule that exists today to shape a manifest field against, which is a harder form of the same caution the record already raised, now checked rather than assumed.

Status is rewritten to keep the record open to revisit but name a sharper trigger than plain rule count, since counting rules already fired twice without moving the outcome: revisit when a rule's real contents populate one of the fields with zero instance today (optional enhanced implementation, external diagnostic mapping, correction/suppression contract, evaluation corpus, or agent-guidance fragments) for the first time, or when a fifth rule's required-capability shape or applicability semantics is found to reconverge with an existing rule rather than adding a third variant.

Preservation: cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-validate passes with NOMOS_V14_CORPUS, NOMOS_SPEC_ARCHIVES and NOMOS_RUST_CORPUS all set (not corpus-unset only).

items.title: crates/README.md claims one directory per band; the tree has folders spanning several
items.why: crates/README.md and its folder-organization comment both state 'one directory per dependency band, which is the workspace's architecture.' crates/substrate/ alone holds nomos-workspace(18), nomos-ledger(20), nomos-capability(21) and nomos-analysis(22) -- four bands under one directory -- so the claim is false against the real tree. items.title: nomos-cli composes gate run because gate-orchestration and check-orchestration are peer bands, a seam OD-HOST-002 does not yet record
items.why: OD-HOST-002 surveys nine state families and records WorkCommand, CheckCommand and SpecCommand seams as closed, but never mentions the run verb GateCommand gained -- family 9 predates it. crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/run.rs documents why itself: nomos-gate-orchestration and nomos-check-orchestration are both band 40 (README.md), and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs Test_Dependencies_Should_Run_Strictly_Downward forbids a band depending on its own band, so the walk-judge-reduce composition for nomos gate run lives in nomos-cli instead of nomos-gate-orchestration. A second adapter wanting gate run without depending on nomos-cli -- exactly the API/MCP parity ARC-ROADMAP-001 names as near-term, next to Gate policy itself -- would have to re-derive that composition, the same duplication OD-HOST-001 fixed for the work group before a second adapter existed. Grepped directly: nothing else at band 40 depends on nomos-gate-orchestration, so moving it above nomos-check-orchestration band costs nothing else in the workspace.
items.done_when: nomos-gate-orchestration exposes a public function generic over nomos-platform traits (the same genericity nomos_check_orchestration::Run and nomos_work_orchestration::Run already have) that, given an already-walked source set, composes nomos_check_orchestration::Run and the Disposition function this crate already owns into a GateRunResult -- the same value crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/run.rs currently builds by hand. nomos-gate-orchestration band moves above nomos-check-orchestration band so that dependency satisfies the strictly-downward rule, and README.md band table and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs BANDS agree. crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/run.rs shrinks to the directory walk and platform construction only, calling the new function instead of duplicating its logic. tests/contract/surface/nomos-gate-orchestration.txt is regenerated against the new public surface. OD-HOST-002 gains an amendment recording the GateCommand run verb as a closed seam, alongside the existing SpecCommand amendment, and diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered and pass their freshness checks.

Declined.reason: Splitting: the code seam needs no spec-store territory, and a live peer holds crates/spec/nomos-spec-store for ~3h; re-authoring as two disjoint items so the code half is claimable now.

items.title: MemoryFactStore::Invalidate stops cloning the whole dependents map, by splitting into two passes
items.why: OD-ANALYSIS-008 named the clone's O(whole store) cost as a real, accepted hazard, and named its own fix option 2 -- restructure Invalidate into two passes without touching DependencyPropagation at all -- as 'a real candidate for a future item' precisely because it does not touch the seam D-130/D-138 care about matching against a second implementation. The user's roadmap override covers incremental-analysis performance hardening, but this fix does not even need it: it changes no public seam, only MemoryFactStore's own internal walk.
items.done_when: MemoryFactStore::Invalidate no longer clones self.dependents. Propagate (fact/memory_store/invalidation.rs) becomes two passes: pass one calls DependencyPropagation::Spread with a real immutable borrow of store.dependents and a callback that only reads (via a new MemoryFactStore::Already_Invalidated, the read-only half of what Invalidate_One already checks) to decide whether to keep spreading and to collect the accepted digests; pass two, after the walk and its borrow have ended, calls Invalidate_One and writes report.dependent for each collected digest. The reasoning that makes the split sound (a digest is visited exactly once per call, so no digest's Already_Invalidated read can be stale from a mutation this same call made to a different digest) is written down beside the new function, not left implicit. Every existing invalidation test in fact/memory_store/tests.rs continues to pass unmodified, proving the observable InvalidationReport is unchanged. DependencyPropagation's trait signature in propagation.rs is untouched. OD-ANALYSIS-008 gains an amendment recording this fix and that its own seam-facing option remains open.

items.title: nomos gate explain: a first real body for ARC-ROADMAP-001's third named verb
items.why: ARC-ROADMAP-001 names plan/run/explain/compare as Gate's four verbs; plan and run are real, explain and compare have no variant at all yet, the same 'no invented shape ahead of a real body' discipline this crate documents. The user's roadmap override covers Gate's run/explain/compare verbs by name. explain is the smaller of the two remaining -- answering one named finding's fate needs no stored-baseline concept the way compare (comparing two runs) would -- so it goes first, the same plan-then-run sequencing this crate already used.
items.done_when: nomos-gate-orchestration gains Explain_Gate: judges walked exactly as Run_Gate does (a shared Judged helper factored out of both, so the two do not duplicate the walk/empty/unreadable match), then answers a FindingQuery (rule: RuleId, location: String -- the same human-visible locations a Finding already carries, no digest exposed to a human) against what was judged. The answer is an Explanation: NotFound, or Found { finding, would_block, suppressed_by } where would_block is Finding::Can_Fail_A_Build with no SuppressionPolicy match and suppressed_by names the match if any. Explicitly independent of GateCommand::scope/rules -- explain answers what one finding looks like right now, not what a scope- or rule-narrowed run would currently see -- documented as that deliberate asymmetry, not an oversight. nomos gate explain --root <path> --rule <id> --location <path> is wired through nomos-cli's GateInvocation, parsing and report, reusing existing ExitCode variants (Ok for not-found or found-but-not-blocking, Violations for found-and-would-block, Contradictory/Vacuous matching run's own unreadable/no-source cases) rather than adding a new one. Surface snapshot reblessed.

items.title: work add cannot declare a predicate's timeout, so a corpus-reaching territory can never produce a verdict
items.why: P13-CLEANFILE-SUBSTRATE's predicate (cargo test -p nomos-ledger -p nomos-analysis -p nomos-capability -p nomos-workspace) stalls at exactly 300s every time: nomos-workspace::tests::portable::over_the_corpus::Test_A_Hundred_Ingestion_Orders_Should_Yield_Byte_Identical_Queries legitimately runs ~469s silent against the real F:/repos/xvpe corpus (5000+ members, 100 permutations) before printing anything, and OD-PLATFORM-001 (P13-LEDGER-IDLE-BOUND-2) fixes the idle bound at half the wall bound. P11-EXEC-IDLE already named a bigger timeout as the only remedy for this exact tension, but DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600 in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/verification/predicate.rs is not exposed by nomos-cli's work add (crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/parse.rs), so no newly authored item can ever choose a timeout that fits a corpus-backed predicate. Confirmed twice directly: work finish on P13-CLEANFILE-SUBSTRATE reported Stalled { idle_elapsed: 300.00s } both times, with the same predicate run standalone taking 469.39s and passing cleanly.
items.done_when: nomos work add exposes a way to declare a predicate's timeout_seconds above the 600s default, and re-running P13-CLEANFILE-SUBSTRATE's exact predicate (or a successor item with the same territory) through nomos work finish with an adjusted timeout produces a real verdict instead of the Stalled conflict.

Grepped directly: nothing outside nomos-gate-orchestration's own crate and nomos-cli calls Run_Gate today, except nomos-ledger's internal gate step (crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/finish/gate_step.rs), which is an internal composition inside the work-finish flow, not an external-facing adapter. The user's standing roadmap override (recorded after the seam itself was built) names 'an actual API/MCP adapter calling the seam' as unblocked work, not still waiting for a trigger. items.title: OD-WORKFLOW-001: the workflow tier's first real increment is RunId's first consumer, not the engine
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names headless workflow orchestration as a near-term-tier item, and the user's standing roadmap override names it as unblocked work, not still waiting for a trigger. Read directly against the v14 corpus (NOMOS_V14_CORPUS's requirements directory): WF-001 through WF-012 and WF-ORDER-001 through WF-ORDER-005 describe a real execution engine -- deterministic branch/merge semantics and bounded parallelism (WF-010), retries that must not repeat non-idempotent effects without a compensation or deduplication token (WF-012), workflow definitions versioned independently from runs with historical replay pinning the exact definition/packages/providers/environment/inputs/approval decisions (WF-011), immutable published artifacts (WF-009), and a WorkflowStep contract (WF-008) with eleven distinct declared properties. Every one of those is a real subsystem or multi-field contract with zero existing implementation anywhere in this workspace to check a shape against -- the same absence OD-PACKAGE-008 already measured for RulePackage's manifest fields, at a larger scale, and this workspace has repeatedly declined to design a seam ahead of a second real case (OD-PACKAGE-006, OD-PACKAGE-008, nomos-gate-orchestration's own doc on why compare is not stubbed).

Grepped directly: crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/identity.rs already declares RunId ("Identity of one execution of a workflow or gate"), present since this crate's first commit, and its only reference anywhere in the workspace outside identity.rs itself is its own re-export in nomos-contracts's lib.rs -- nothing constructs one. nomos_gate_orchestration::GateRunResult, this workspace's one real shipped "one execution" today, carries no run identity of its own.

Rather than invent WorkflowStep or any part of the engine blind, this item authors OD-WORKFLOW-001: the workflow tier's first real, defensible increment is giving RunId -- vocabulary this workspace already committed to, naming exactly the "workflow or gate" split this tier needs -- its first real consumer via Gate, the one real "one execution" that exists, and deciding the one open design question a follow-up implementation needs answered (content-addressed versus per-execution identity) before nomos-gate-orchestration::Run_Gate's signature is touched. It builds no code against a shipped, multiply-depended-on seam (nomos-cli, nomos-ledger and nomos-api all call Run_Gate today) -- that is a separate, later claimed item, the same record-then-code split OD-GATE-014's override record and P13-GATE-014-SCOPE-RULE-SELECTORS already used.

items.title: OD-WORKFLOW-001: the workflow tier's first real increment is RunId's first consumer, not the engine
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names headless workflow orchestration as a near-term-tier item, and the user's standing roadmap override names it as unblocked work, not still waiting for a trigger. Read directly against the v14 corpus (NOMOS_V14_CORPUS's requirements directory): WF-001 through WF-012 and WF-ORDER-001 through WF-ORDER-005 describe a real execution engine -- deterministic branch/merge semantics and bounded parallelism (WF-010), retries that must not repeat non-idempotent effects without a compensation or deduplication token (WF-012), workflow definitions versioned independently from runs with historical replay pinning the exact definition/packages/providers/environment/inputs/approval decisions (WF-011), immutable published artifacts (WF-009), and a WorkflowStep contract (WF-008) with eleven distinct declared properties. Every one of those is a real subsystem or multi-field contract with zero existing implementation anywhere in this workspace to check a shape against -- the same absence OD-PACKAGE-008 already measured for RulePackage's manifest fields, at a larger scale, and this workspace has repeatedly declined to design a seam ahead of a second real case (OD-PACKAGE-006, OD-PACKAGE-008, nomos-gate-orchestration's own doc on why compare is not stubbed).

Grepped directly: crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/identity.rs already declares RunId ("Identity of one execution of a workflow or gate"), present since this crate's first commit, and its only reference anywhere in the workspace outside identity.rs itself is its own re-export in nomos-contracts's lib.rs -- nothing constructs one. nomos_gate_orchestration::GateRunResult, this workspace's one real shipped "one execution" today, carries no run identity of its own.

Rather than invent WorkflowStep or any part of the engine blind, this item authors OD-WORKFLOW-001: the workflow tier's first real, defensible increment is giving RunId -- vocabulary this workspace already committed to, naming exactly the "workflow or gate" split this tier needs -- its first real consumer via Gate, the one real "one execution" that exists, and deciding the one open design question a follow-up implementation needs answered (content-addressed versus per-execution identity) before nomos-gate-orchestration::Run_Gate's signature is touched. It builds no code against a shipped, multiply-depended-on seam (nomos-cli, nomos-ledger and nomos-api all call Run_Gate today) -- that is a separate, later claimed item, the same record-then-code split OD-GATE-014's override record and P13-GATE-014-SCOPE-RULE-SELECTORS already used.
items.done_when: docs/records/OD-WORKFLOW-001-the-workflow-tiers-first-real-increment-is-runids-first-consumer-not-the-engine.md exists, accepted, authority canonical-normative-record, and decides: (1) the workflow tier's first real increment is RunId's first real consumer through Gate, not WorkflowStep or any part of the WF-009..WF-012 execution engine; (2) RunId identifies one execution, not one configuration -- not a pure content digest of GateCommand and the build variant, since two runs of an identical command are two different executions and WF-005's own text keeps cache hits distinct from a run's own identity; (3) the follow-up implementation this record unblocks (not built by this item) threads a nomos_platform::Clock parameter into nomos_gate_orchestration::Run_Gate alongside its existing ProcessLauncher one, and gives GateRunResult a pub run: RunId field computed from that clock reading. crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-WORKFLOW-001.record registers the record's path so it is governing, not merely written. diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered (nomos spec render --profile diagram-set --into . and --profile domain-specification --into .) against a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes, and are current. No code in nomos-gate-orchestration, nomos-cli, nomos-ledger or nomos-api is touched by this item.

items.title: OD-WORKFLOW-001's clock-only RunId plan is stale: Timestamp's own doc rules it out before code was written
items.why:
OD-WORKFLOW-001's "Concretely, for the follow-up" paragraph (docs/records/OD-WORKFLOW-001-...) says a follow-up should compute RunId "once per call from the clock reading (and nothing else content-addressed)". Checking nomos_platform::Timestamp's own module doc before any code was written against this plan (crates/platform/nomos-platform/src/clock/timestamp.rs): "Second resolution is deliberate ... Where ordering matters more finely than a second, the ordering is carried explicitly rather than inferred from a clock." A RunId computed purely from clock.Now() therefore collides for any two runs starting within the same wall-clock second -- not a rare case: nomos-api's own test suite calls Handle_Gate_Run twice inside one process well under a second apart, and .github/workflows/gate.yml runs multiple gate-adjacent steps in quick succession. Grepped directly: no Random or nonce port exists anywhere in crates/platform, and the workspace's root Cargo.toml carries no rand or uuid dependency -- adding one is its own decision, subject to cargo-deny's advisories/bans/licenses/sources check, out of scope for a record naming a first increment.

Building Run_Gate's signature change against the unchecked plan would have shipped a RunId that fails its own record's stated purpose (distinguishing two real executions) the first time two runs land in the same second, which is routine rather than rare. This item corrects the record before that code is written, the same "found wrong before code caught up" pattern P13-GATE-014-RULE-COUNT-STALE-3 and P13-CLI-CARGO-GATE-COMMENT-STALE already used for a stale record.
items.done_when: docs/records/OD-WORKFLOW-001-the-workflow-tiers-first-real-increment-is-runids-first-consumer-not-the-engine.md is amended to version 2: an appended "Amendment" section withdraws the Clock-parameter/digest-of-clock-reading plan, states the concrete reason (Timestamp's own module doc names second resolution as deliberate and finer ordering as carried explicitly rather than inferred from a clock), and replaces it with the corrected plan -- Run_Gate accepts a caller-supplied run: RunId value parameter (no Clock dependency, no new generic), each composition root constructs its own RunId however it can, and the honest first-increment construction is a new nomos_contracts::RunId::Fresh(now: Timestamp) associated function combining the clock reading, std::process::id() (already used this way for scratch-path uniqueness in this workspace's own tests), and a process-local monotonic counter -- named as collision-free within one process and reduced-but-not-eliminated across processes, not claimed as perfect. The original "Concretely, for the follow-up" paragraph is left in place (not deleted), the same append-only amendment shape OD-HOST-002 already uses, so the record's own history of what it once said stays legible. `nomos spec preview --id OD-WORKFLOW-001 --from <the edited file>` reports no lost blocks or relations. diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered from a clean worktree carrying exactly this commit's registered records and are current.

items.title: OD-WORKFLOW-001 wrongly lists nomos-ledger as a Run_Gate caller -- Run_Gate_Step is a different function
items.why:
OD-WORKFLOW-001's "Concretely, for the follow-up" paragraph (docs/records/OD-WORKFLOW-001-...) lists nomos-ledger's finish/gate_step.rs among Run_Gate's callers ("Every existing caller of Run_Gate (nomos-cli's gate.rs, nomos-ledger's finish/gate_step.rs, nomos-api's Handle_Gate_Run) supplies a real clock"). Checking that file directly (crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/finish/gate_step.rs) rather than trusting an earlier substring grep for "Run_Gate": its function is Run_Gate_Step, a distinct name that only contains "Run_Gate" as a substring. Run_Gate_Step reads the workflow's own LINT_STEP argv and runs it directly through a ProcessLauncher (crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/finish.rs:110) -- nomos work finish's own pre-flight lint check, unrelated to nomos_gate_orchestration::Run_Gate, which nomos-ledger never calls or imports anywhere. Grepped again to confirm: no occurrence of nomos_gate_orchestration or the literal token Run_Gate (not Run_Gate_Step) exists anywhere under crates/substrate/nomos-ledger. There are exactly two real callers of Run_Gate in this workspace today: nomos-cli's gate.rs and nomos-api's Handle_Gate_Run.

This does not change OD-WORKFLOW-001's decision or its amendment's corrected plan -- both survive with nomos-ledger simply removed from the caller list -- but a governing record asserting a grepped fact that turns out false undermines the same "grepped directly" credibility this record and its neighbors repeatedly lean on, and a future session building the Run_Gate/RunId follow-up would otherwise update a fourth caller that does not exist.

items.title: Fresh_Run_Id and a real run: RunId on GateRunResult, per OD-WORKFLOW-001
items.why:
OD-WORKFLOW-001 (version 3, accepted) names this exact follow-up as unblocked, real code: give nomos_gate_orchestration::GateRunResult a real RunId, computed per-execution rather than as a content digest of the command. Its amendment corrected the original clock-only plan (Timestamp is deliberately second-resolution per its own module doc) to a caller-supplied RunId value plus a first-increment RunId::Fresh construction combining a clock reading, the process id, and a process-local counter.

Checked against the real dependency-band constraints before writing code (the record's own text named the construction as living in nomos-contracts, which this item corrects in the doing rather than the record, since it is a code-shape detail the record's own "does not implement" clause already left to the implementation): nomos-contracts is band 0 and may depend on nothing but serde (OD-CONTRACTS-001, enforced by Test_Contracts_Should_Depend_On_The_Allowlist_And_Nothing_Else), so it cannot take a nomos_platform::Timestamp parameter or use nomos_model::Digest_Of_Parts. nomos-model is band 10 and nomos-platform is band 15, so nomos-model cannot depend on nomos-platform either. The only band-legal home for a function needing both a real clock reading and Digest_Of_Parts is nomos-gate-orchestration itself (band 41), which already depends on nomos-platform and gains nomos-model as a real (not dev-only) dependency here.

Grepped directly: exactly two real callers of nomos_gate_orchestration::Run_Gate exist in this workspace -- nomos-cli's gate.rs and nomos-api's Handle_Gate_Run (nomos-ledger's Run_Gate_Step, OD-WORKFLOW-001's own correction already established, is unrelated). Both already depend on nomos-platform-std for StdProcessLauncher; nomos-cli already depends on nomos-platform too, nomos-api gains it here for the Clock trait.
items.done_when: nomos-gate-orchestration exports a new pub fn Fresh_Run_Id(now: nomos_platform::Timestamp) -> nomos_contracts::RunId, combining now.Unix_Seconds(), std::process::id() and a process-local monotonic AtomicU64 counter through nomos_model::Digest_Of_Parts into RunId::From_Digest -- documented as collision-free within one process and reduced-but-not-eliminated across processes, not claimed as more. nomos_gate_orchestration::Run_Gate gains a run: RunId parameter (a plain caller-supplied value, no Clock generic, no internal computation) and nomos_gate_orchestration::GateRunResult gains a pub run: RunId field, set from that parameter. Every existing call site in crates/orchestration/nomos-gate-orchestration/src/tests.rs is updated to pass one (a fixed test RunId is fine there; a real Fresh_Run_Id call is not required in every test). crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate.rs's GateInvocation::Run arm calls Fresh_Run_Id(SystemClock.Now()) and passes it to Run_Gate. crates/host/nomos-api/src/lib.rs's Handle_Gate_Run does the same, and crates/host/nomos-api/src/response.rs's GateRunResponse gains a pub run: RunId field carried from GateRunResult::run (RunId already derives Serialize). nomos-gate-orchestration's Cargo.toml moves nomos-model from dev-dependencies to dependencies; nomos-api's Cargo.toml gains nomos-platform. tests/contract/surface/nomos-gate-orchestration.txt and tests/contract/surface/nomos-api.txt are regenerated (NOMOS_SURFACE_BLESS) and current. nomos-cli's gate/report.rs text rendering is unchanged -- this increment does not add RunId to the CLI's printed output, only to the typed result. nomos-contracts is not touched: RunId's existing From_Digest/Digest accessors are sufficient and no new method is added there.

items.title: OD-CORRECTIONS-001: corrections has real staging machinery and zero real callers
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names corrections as a near-term-tier item, and the user's standing roadmap override names it unblocked, not still waiting for a trigger. Grepped directly: nothing outside crates/corrections/nomos-corrections itself and tests/integration/tests/determinism (which only checks CorrectionStaging's determinism declaration, not real usage) references nomos_corrections anywhere in this workspace -- zero real callers, matching the "corrections product workflow" gap the roadmap override names.

Read in full before drafting any code (candidate.rs, plan.rs, staged.rs, validated.rs, committed.rs, determinism.rs): the crate is not empty scaffolding. CorrectionPlan::New already refuses two candidates touching the same path (COR-003's "planned as a compatible set", read from the v14 corpus's COR-001..COR-013 family, volume-05.7-3-corrections-and-convergence); StagedPlan::Of already refuses a candidate whose declared prior content does not match the live workspace; ValidatedPlan::Commit and CommittedPlan::Rollback already submit through and reverse through nomos_workspace::Workspace's one real door, checking at every step that the workspace has not moved since the previous one (Assert_Not_Moved, shared by all three). This is a real, tested implementation of COR-005's first half (stage, validate, commit or refuse).

What is not built, checked against the same COR family: COR-005's second half (rerun affected rules, compare state signatures after commit -- ValidatedPlan::Commit does not call back into nomos-check-orchestration or nomos-rules at all); COR-006 (oscillation/divergence/stall detection, which needs a caller loop that does not exist since nothing calls this crate); COR-001/COR-010 (classifying a candidate as mechanical, proposed, agent, or interactive); COR-011..COR-013 (ranking, arbitration, objective weights). The crate's own module doc states this omission is deliberate: "No agent and no model backend appears anywhere in this crate... what a candidate would do is decided before this crate exists to run it" -- this crate is scoped to the mechanical executor half only, by its own design, not by an oversight this item would be filling in.

Checked against the one real candidate for "what decides what to fix": this workspace's four shipped rules (Check_Completeness_Mirrors, Check_Naming_Convention, Check_Dependency_Direction, Check_Unread_Reaches_A_Finding). None produces a violation with a safe, judgment-free fix today -- Check_Naming_Convention's own violation (a function name against README.md's Pascal_Snake_Case convention) would need every call site renamed in step to stay correct, which is a real refactor requiring semantic understanding this workspace has no infrastructure for, not a mechanical edit. OD-PACKAGE-008 already measured the same absence from a different angle: "the complete absence... of any real instance of ... a correction and suppression contract... with zero real shape to build a manifest field against anywhere in the workspace today."

Building a CorrectionCandidate generator now would mean inventing either a fix for a rule that has none safely available, or the classification/ranking layer (COR-001, COR-010-013) that has no real case to check its shape against -- the same "no invented shape ahead of a real body" caution this workspace applies repeatedly (OD-PACKAGE-006, OD-PACKAGE-008, nomos-gate-orchestration's own doc on why compare is not stubbed). items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names model backend and agent executor infrastructure as a near-term-tier item. The user explicitly overrode the population-of-zero caution OD-PACKAGE-006/OD-PACKAGE-008 apply elsewhere (no real ModelBackend or AgentExecutor implementation exists anywhere in this workspace to check a manifest shape against) after being asked directly whether to build this now, do a performance audit instead, or stop -- chose to build it now, in the same terms nomos-lang-package's own creation used for LanguagePackage: OD-PACKAGE-001 scoped that crate to "the first manifest maturity," explicitly deferring PKG-022's larger field list (recognition, file mappings, capability claims, canonical mappings, environment requirements, projections, quality objectives, conformance suites) to later. This record draws the same boundary for ModelBackendPackage/AgentExecutorPackage.

Read directly from NOMOS_V14_CORPUS's requirements directory: MODEL-ROUTE-037 through MODEL-ROUTE-049 describe a mature model-routing system -- resolution invalidation on catalog/entitlement/capability change (044), a normative RoutingPolicyConformanceSuite with deterministic fixtures (045-047), preserved conformance results with resolution hashes and semantic diffs (048), and conformance gates at publication/release/canary (049). None of it has any real implementation to check a shape against, and building it now would be pure invention with no second real case, the same OD-PACKAGE-008 already-tested caution -- the override authorizes building something now, not building everything. MODEL-ROUTE-037's own opening clause is the one piece with a bounded, statable shape: "Every ModelBackendPackage and AgentExecutorPackage shall expose a versioned discovered model catalog or explicitly declare that model selection is opaque or executor-controlled."

Read in full before drafting any code: crates/packages/nomos-package's real shape (PackageManifest, Parse_Manifest, ProviderRegistration) and crates/packages/nomos-lang-package's real shape, the one existing precedent for a second PackageKind's manifest maturity. It has proven this for Gate (Run_Gate) but not for any of the other three closed OD-HOST-001/002 seams -- grepped directly: nomos_work_orchestration::Run has exactly one real caller in this workspace, crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs, and nothing else, including nomos-api, calls it. This is the same "declared and deliberately unconsumed by a second caller" gap nomos-api was built to close for Gate, now real for Work too.

WorkOutcome::List(BoardView) wraps nomos_ledger::LedgerDocument, which already derives Serialize/Deserialize (it is the type ledger.json itself round-trips through) -- so, unlike GateRunResult, no new serializable projection type is needed here; the real type is JSON-ready already.

items.title: nomos-api gains a fifth real seam: Work's Validate verb
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has proven a second real caller for Gate::run, Work::List, Spec::Profiles and Work::Show. crates/orchestration/nomos-work-orchestration/src/run.rs's own doc groups WorkCommand's eleven verbs by what Run needs to execute them: "List, Show, Validate and Audit need nothing but ledger" -- the same zero-extra-composition shape List and Show already proved reachable from this crate. Validate is the next of that group with no seam: grepped directly, nomos_work_orchestration::Run's WorkCommand::Validate arm has exactly one real caller in this workspace, crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs's Report_Validation.

Checked before authoring: unlike List and Show, Validate is not a read reflected back -- run.rs's own Validated() helper loads the document, runs nomos_ledger::Validate(&document, now) and, on any violation, returns Err(LedgerError::Invalid{violations}) rather than Ok. So this is a real new capability for nomos-api, not a second view onto data List already exposes: a wire caller gets a genuine internal-consistency check, with the violation list folded into LedgerError's Display (the same string-the-error shape WorkListResponse::Unreadable already uses for a LedgerError that does not derive Serialize).
items.done_when: nomos-api gains a new public function Handle_Work_Validate(directory: \&Path) -> WorkValidateResponse, calling nomos_work_orchestration::Run(\&WorkCommand::Validate, \&mut ledger, \&StdProcessLauncher, published) with the same FileLedger::At/StdFileSystem/SystemClock/FileLock composition and the same unreached empty Territory::Of_Files closure for published that Handle_Work_List and Handle_Work_Show already use (WorkCommand::Validate never reaches it). WorkValidateResponse is a tagged Valid{document: nomos_ledger::LedgerDocument} / Invalid{cause: String} enum, the same two-state honesty shape WorkListResponse::{Listed,Unreadable} already establishes -- Invalid names both a genuine ledger-invariant violation and an unreadable file alike, exactly as nomos_ledger::LedgerError::Invalid and its other variants already collapse under one Display, so no finer split is invented here than the type underneath already draws. A real test proves this crate can validate a real, well-formed scratch ledger it writes itself (the same process-id-scoped std::env::temp_dir() pattern the existing Work tests use) and asserts Valid. A second test proves a scratch ledger carrying a real invariant violation (two items whose territory overlaps, the same fixture shape nomos-ledger's own Validate tests use) returns Invalid with a non-empty cause naming the violation. A third test proves the Valid response round-trips through serde_json. tests/contract/surface/nomos-api.txt is regenerated (NOMOS_SURFACE_BLESS) and current. nomos-work-orchestration, nomos-ledger and nomos-cli are not touched by this item.
